items.title: xtouch-daemon
items.text: xtouch-daemon turns a Behringer X-Touch Extender into a hardware mixer for PipeWire on Linux. Its motor faders, LED meters and scribble strips control your devices and applications. A strip can also belong to Home Assistant instead, for lights, speakers in other rooms or scenes.

items.title: Strips
items.text:
• Device strips (output, input) control an output or an input, or whatever is the default. Select makes the device the default, and its LED shows which one is. See Devices.
  • Several devices on one strip: a list or a * wildcard (e.g. bluez_output.* for any Bluetooth headphones). The strip shows the one that is there, and Select switches between them.
  • Sound card profiles: Rec switches the card between profiles, e.g. analog and digital output. The label of the active profile names the strip, and each profile can have its own volume range.
  • Application strips (apps) control all streams of a group of applications at once, e.g. every browser. A stream that starts later gets the strip's volume. See Applications.
  • Auto strips (auto) pick up the next application that plays and has no strip of its own. They keep it for a few seconds after it stops, so it does not jump between strips from track to track. The encoder picks another application, a push pins it. Aliases give applications readable names.
  • Home Assistant strips (homeassistant) turn a strip into entities for your automations over MQTT discovery: the motor fader, the encoder, the LCD lines and color, the LEDs, and events for every button press. See Home Assistant.
  • Empty strips (empty) stay dark and do nothing.

items.title: On every strip
items.text:
• Motor faders glide to new values smoothly, follow changes made anywhere else, and stay still while your finger is on them. Only a touched fader changes a value.
  • Volume ranges: the fader covers min_volume to max_volume, up to 200 % (amplified in software). See Strips.
  • Scribble strips show a label and the volume (or muted, idle, off) on a backlight in the strip's color. A strip whose device or applications are not there goes dark.
  • Mute button with LED.
  • Encoder modes: the encoder sets the balance, fine-tunes the volume, picks the application of an auto strip, or seeks and plays/pauses the media player of the applications. Its LED ring shows what it controls.
  • Home Assistant controls on audio strips: the encoder (or the fader) becomes an entity in Home Assistant, e.g. to dim a light, while the other control keeps the volume. See Encoders.
  • Rec and Solo LEDs as indicators: recording, playing, default or muted. See LEDs.
  • LED meters show the level of each strip, before or after its fader (meter_point), and light their red LED for half a second when the audio clips (a peak at full scale). They are passive: they never wake a device, never light your desktop's microphone indicator, and never switch Bluetooth headphones into headset mode.

items.title: Around it
items.text:
• GUI editor (xtouch-daemon gui): the eight strips as the device shows them right now, editing with errors next to the options, suggestions from the sound server, drag to reorder, undo, "Try on the device" that runs the unsaved changes on the device, and save-and-apply that keeps the comments of the file. See GUI.
  • Command line tools: a device self-test, lists of devices, profiles and applications, a configuration check. See Commands.
  • Robust: survives unplugging or switching off the device and restarts of the sound server and the MQTT broker, and shows everything again when they are back.
  • A proper service: a systemd user service with readiness notification (Type=notify). systemctl --user reload applies a changed configuration without a restart, and the log goes to the journal with levels. Startup and shutdown sequences light the strips up and turn them dark: one after the other, all at once, like a curtain or behind a wave of light. When it stops, it leaves the surface dark.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Linux with PipeWire and pipewire-pulse (or PulseAudio).
  • pw-record (part of PipeWire) for the meters.
  • Python 3.14.
  • A Behringer X-Touch Extender in MC mode on USB (see Getting started).
  • For Home Assistant strips: an MQTT broker that Home Assistant uses (e.g. the Mosquitto add-on).

items.title: Where to go next
items.text: Section What it covers Getting started Install, set up and test the device, write a first configuration, run the service; or try it without a device. Guides The GUI, Home Assistant, Mumble, and Troubleshooting. Configuration The file, applying changes, and every option: channels, states and slots, the channel types, the parts of a strip. Reference Every command, the hardware and its protocol, the voice chat bridge. Development How it works inside (Architecture) and why (Design documents).

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
xtouch-daemon reads a TOML file, by default ~/.config/xtouch-daemon/config.toml ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME is respected). -c FILE selects another one. Without a file at the default path it uses the example configuration: six auto slots, the default input and the default output.

xtouch-daemon init-config      # writes the example to the default path (-f overwrites)
xtouch-daemon check-config     # validates the file and shows what each slot shows when

Unknown options are errors, so a typo does not go unnoticed. check-config names the place of every error, e.g. channel.mic.label: String should have at most 7 characters.

The GUI edits the same options in a window and shows the same errors next to them.

items.title: Sections
items.text:
Section What it configures Page [channel.<id>] What a strip can control: a device, a group of applications, a person, Home Assistant. Channels [slots] What each strip of the device (a slot) shows, and when. Channels, states and slots [state.<id>] States and modes (in a call, gaming) that the slots ask about. Channels, states and slots [controls] Actions of the buttons, fader or encoder of a slot, whatever it shows. Channels, states and slots [pool.apps], [pool.auto] How apps and auto take the next application that plays. Applications [pool.people], [voip] The people of the voice chat, and where they sit. People [pool.devices] Outputs and inputs without a channel (a USB headset) on the slots that name devices. Devices [device] Which sound card is the extender. Behavior [behavior] Volume limit, encoder step, reset volume, meters. Behavior [aliases] Names to show for applications on auto slots. Behavior [switching] The chord and the banner of a new mode. Channels, states and slots [mqtt] The MQTT broker of Home Assistant. Home Assistant

The channel types:

type What the channel controls Page output, input An output or an input device, several of them, choices to switch between, or the default one. Devices apps All streams of a group of applications. Applications person Someone of the voice chat. People homeassistant Nothing by itself: its parts are entities in Home Assistant. Home Assistant

In a slot, apps is the next application that plays and has no channel of its own (Applications), people the next person of the voice chat (People), auto either, and - a dark strip (Channels).

items.title: Applying changes
items.text:
xtouch-daemon check-config && systemctl --user reload xtouch-daemon

A reload (SIGHUP) takes the new file without a restart: slots whose strip stays the same keep it. A file with errors is reported in the log and the current configuration stays.

Two sections need a restart (systemctl --user restart xtouch-daemon):

  • A changed [device] name or virtual. A reload takes the rest of the file, but keeps the old device.
  • A changed [mqtt] section. Until the restart, a reload keeps the whole current configuration.

The GUI applies a saved file the same way: it reloads the running daemon (the service, or one started from a terminal or an IDE), or offers a restart. It then tells whether the daemon took the file.

items.title: Behavior, device and aliases
items.text: The sections that apply to the daemon and to every strip. The GUI shows them in the tab "Global settings".

items.title: [device]
items.text:
Option Default Meaning name "X-Touch-Ext" Part of the name of the extender's sound card, as /proc/asound/cards lists it. virtual false Drive the virtual device instead of the real one (xtouch-daemon run --virtual-device does the same for one run). touch_required true Whether a fader changes a value only while the device reports a touch. false makes every move count, see below. touchless_faders [] Faders whose touch sensor does not work, numbered from 1 on the left, see below. startup "sweep" How the strips light up after a connect, see below. shutdown "sweep" How the strips go dark when the daemon stops, see below.

A reload takes them all: with another name or virtual the daemon lets go of the device and connects to the other one, which shows the same.

items.title: Startup and shutdown sequences
items.text:
After a connect the strips light up and their faders come up to their values; when the daemon stops, the strips go dark and their faders go down. startup and shutdown choose how:

Value Startup Shutdown instant All strips at once. All strips at once. sweep One after the other from the left, 80 ms apart. One after the other from the right. curtain From the middle outwards, pair by pair (4 and 5 first, 1 and 8 last). From the outside in. show A wave of light runs across from the left: each strip lights up white with all its buttons, its meter jumps to the top and falls, its ring fills up. Behind the wave the strips show what they are, about 1.2 s after the connect. From the right, each strip flashes white, its meter jumps to the top and its ring drains; then it goes dark. 
[device]
startup = "show"
shutdown = "curtain"

items.title: Faders without a touch sensor
items.text:
Only a touched fader changes a value (see Hardware), so a fader whose touch sensor failed goes back to its value shortly after every move. Until it is repaired, touchless_faders lets it work without the sensor: a move counts as a touch, and half a second without a move as letting go. In the GUI these are the buttons under "Touchless faders" on the page "Device".

[device]
touchless_faders = [1]   # the touch sensor of fader 1 is broken

touch_required = false does the same for all faders. The touch sensor does not notice everything that moves a fader on purpose, e.g. a fingertip pushing it from below; with it off, such a push counts too.

[device]
touch_required = false   # every move of a fader counts

What it can't do:

  • Resting fingers: a finger that rests on the fader without moving it counts as gone after half a second. The fader then goes to its value, which is where the finger left it, so you notice nothing, unless the value changes elsewhere meanwhile.
  • The first 3 seconds after a connect: after it was switched on, the device moves its faders down by itself. So in the first 3 seconds after the device was connected, a move counts only with a touch, like on the other faders.

items.title: [behavior]
items.text:
Option Default Meaning max_volume 130 The volume of a fader at the top, 100..200 percent. Above 100 % the audio is amplified in software. 130 puts 100 % at the 0 dB mark of the device with one slope over the whole travel; 100 puts it at the top. Channels may have their own range. unity_at 77 Where on the fader 100 % is, 10..95 percent of the travel; the device marks 0 dB at about 77. For strips whose range goes above 100 %, see 100 % at the 0 dB mark. encoder_step 1 Percent per encoder step, 1..10. Used by the volume encoder and by the encoders of homeassistant channels. reset_volume 100 The volume a push on a volume encoder sets, 0..200, at most max_volume. It stays within the range of the channel. meters true Whether the LED meters show audio levels at all. The meter option of a channel turns off a single one. meter_point "pre_fader" Where the meters take the level: "pre_fader" before the volume and Mute of each strip, "post_fader" after them. A channel or a place in a slot may have its own, see Meters.

How long apps and auto keep an application and which ones they never take are hold and exclude of [pool.apps].

[behavior]
max_volume = 150
encoder_step = 2
reset_volume = 100

items.title: [aliases]
items.text:
The name to show on an auto slot for an application, at most 7 characters of ASCII:

[aliases]
"WEBRTC VoiceEngine" = "Discord"
"Firefox" = "Firefox"

The key is the application name the sound server reports. xtouch-daemon list-apps shows it, and so do the suggestions of the GUI.

items.title: Presets
items.text:
A preset is a name for a group of well-known applications, so you don't have to look up the names of every browser or the way games show up. Write it with an @ in the lists that match applications, alone or next to names of your own:

[channel.browser]
type = "apps"
label = "Browser"
match = ["@browsers"]

[channel.voip]
type = "apps"
label = "VoIP"
match = ["@voip", "my-voice-app"]

[state.gaming]
mode = true
processes = ["@steam-games"]    # while any game from Steam runs

Presets work in:

  • match of apps channels, apps of states and exclude of [pool.apps]: they match the names and binaries of the applications' streams.
  • processes of states: they match the names of processes.

A preset stands for different names in each: e.g. @steam-games is the streams of Windows games (.exe) in match, and Steam's reaper process in processes. Its names match like the ones you write, as parts of the name, ignoring case. On an apps channel with launch, the processes of its presets count as the application running. An unknown preset is an error that lists the known ones; a preset that can't be used in a list says where it can.

xtouch-daemon check-config shows what each preset stands for, xtouch-daemon list-apps the presets of the applications that play, and the GUI suggests the presets that fit each list.

items.title: The presets
items.text:
Preset What Streams (match, apps, exclude) Processes (processes) @browsers Web browsers firefox, librewolf, floorp, waterfox, zen-bin, chromium, chrome, brave, vivaldi, opera, msedge, epiphany, falkon firefox, librewolf, floorp, waterfox, zen-bin, chromium, brave, vivaldi, opera, msedge, epiphany, falkon @voip Voice and video chats discord, vesktop, webrtc voiceengine, mumble, teamspeak, ts3client, signal, element-desktop, zoom, slack, telegram, jitsi, teams-for-linux discord, vesktop, mumble, teamspeak, ts3client, signal, element-desktop, zoom, slack, telegram, jitsi, teams-for-linux @steam-games Games started from Steam steam_app_, .exe, wine-preloader, wine64-preloader reaper @games Games: from Steam, and any under Wine or Proton (e.g. Lutris, Heroic) steam_app_, .exe, wine-preloader, wine64-preloader reaper, wineserver @music Music players spotify, rhythmbox, strawberry, clementine, elisa, lollypop, amberol, audacious, deadbeef, quod libet, quodlibet, cmus, music player daemon spotify, rhythmbox, strawberry, clementine, elisa, lollypop, amberol, audacious, deadbeef, quodlibet, cmus, mpd @video Video players vlc, mpv, celluloid, totem, kodi, haruna, clapper, mplayer vlc, mpv, celluloid, totem, kodi, haruna, clapper, mplayer
  • @browsers: Electron applications before Electron 40 (e.g. the sounds of Discord) name their streams "Chromium" too. The processes leave out Google Chrome: its process chrome is also part of the name of the crash handler of every Electron application.
  • @voip: Discord talks in a stream of its own, "WEBRTC VoiceEngine".
  • @steam-games: Steam starts every game through its reaper, which runs as long as the game (not the install scripts it runs through it after an update). A stream does not tell who started a game: the streams are those of every game under Wine or Proton. The digital audio workstation REAPER is called reaper too: with it, name the games in processes instead.
  • @games: Lutris and Heroic leave no process of their own while a game runs; wineserver runs while any Windows program runs under Wine or Proton, and a few seconds after it. Native games from Lutris or Heroic are not part of it.

Missing an application? Add its name next to the preset (match = ["@browsers", "netsurf"]), and open an issue, so the preset gets it.

items.title: Channels, states and slots
items.text:
What the device shows: channels are what a strip can control (an output, a group of applications, a person), each strip of the device (a slot) has a short list of the channels it can show, and states (in a call, gaming) decide which. A slot changes only when what it shows changes; the others stay as they are. The design has every detail.

xtouch-daemon init-config writes a small example. xtouch-daemon check-config shows a table of what each slot shows in which states.

items.title: Channels
items.text:
A channel is something a strip controls, with the options of its type (see Channels):

[channel.out]
type = "output"             # or "input": a device, one of several (choices), or the default one
label = "Speaker"

[channel.voip]
type = "apps"               # the streams of a group of applications
match = ["@voip"]
label = "VoIP"

[channel.ann]
type = "person"             # someone of the voice chat, see People
person = ["Ann", "ann-phone"]

[channel.lamp]
type = "homeassistant"      # a strip of Home Assistant automations (needs [mqtt])

The id (out, voip) names the channel in slots, conditions and the entities in Home Assistant.

items.title: Slots
items.text:
[slots]
1 = "out"                                   # always the output
2 = ["voip if call", "auto"]                # the voice chat in a call, else the next application
3 = ["game if gaming", "-"]                 # the game in the mode gaming, else dark
4 = [{ show = "auto", color = "blue" }]     # options of the place
5 = ["people", "apps"]                      # a person of the voice chat, else the next application
  • A slot shows the first candidate whose condition (after if) holds. Conditions name states and modes, with and, or, not, parentheses and present (the channel has something to control); see Conditions.
  • auto is the next application that plays and has no channel of its own, and the people of the voice chat (from the right). apps and people are each of them alone. A slot without an entry is auto, and so is a stack whose candidates all don't hold.
  • - is nothing: the slot is dark.
  • The table form { show = ..., when = ..., ... } takes options of the look at this place (label, color, lit_when_idle, rec, solo, meter, meter_point); on apps and auto also encoder, min_volume and max_volume; on people only color, meter and meter_point.
  • The GUI's page Slots simulates other modes and states (Simulate), in the drawing or on the device.
  • xtouch-daemon why 2 says why slot 2 shows what it shows, xtouch-daemon why voip where the channel is and why.
  • When a slot shows something else, its LCD flashes the new label and why (gaming, not call) for switching.banner seconds.

Four pools are built in: apps (applications, see Applications), people (the people of the voice chat, see People), auto (both) and devices (the outputs and inputs no channel has, see Devices). [pool.apps] has from, hold and exclude, [pool.people] from, order and the look of the strips of people, [pool.auto] the look of the applications on its slots, [pool.devices] from, hold, exclude and the look of the strips of devices.

A pool that has no member for a slot hands it to the pool (or -) right below it: ["people", "apps"] is a person, else an application. A slot that two pools could fill goes to the one higher in its stack.

items.title: States and modes
items.text:
[state.call]
voice_chat = true           # in a channel of the voice chat
recording = ["discord"]     # or: Discord records
delay_off = 5

[state.gaming]
mode = true                 # one mode at a time; without one, "default"
label = "Gaming"            # the banner across the LCDs
processes = ["@steam-games"]

A state is on while any of its sources is: apps (playing), recording, voice_chat, processes, devices, channels, homeassistant (a switch in Home Assistant), or when (a condition of other states). delay_on and delay_off smooth it. Modes are states with mode = true: the one with the highest priority whose sources are on is the mode, else default. When the mode changes, the LCDs show its label across the strips for switching.banner seconds.

apps and processes take parts of names, ignoring case, and presets. For games from Steam, processes = ["@steam-games"] is on while any game runs, native or with Proton: Steam starts every game through its reaper process, which is what the preset stands for. Proton games play as <Game>.exe (e.g. "Planet Crafter.exe"), which apps = ["@games"] catches once they make a sound. Don't use steam (the client runs all the time) or .exe in processes (Wine's helpers, like explorer.exe, run for other Windows programs too). ps -eo comm,args while a game runs shows the names to use for others. Kernel threads don't count.

Every state can be overridden (on, off, auto) from Home Assistant, the GUI's live view or a button; the override lasts until its sources change (persist = true: until it is set back). A mode picked by hand (xtouch-daemon mode gaming, the chord, Home Assistant) lasts until the rules want another one.

items.title: Conditions
items.text:
A condition says when something applies: a candidate of a slot (after if, or when in the table form), a state (when) or controls (when). It holds or not at any moment, and the slot follows at once.

Part Holds while Example a state or mode it is on call, gaming default no other mode is on default present the channel or pool of the candidate has something to control browser if present present(<channel or pool>) that channel or pool has something to control present(game) not <part> the part does not hold not call <part> and <part> both hold call and not gaming <part> or <part> either holds call or present(voip) ( ... ) what is inside holds (call or gaming) and present
  • not binds closest, then and, then or: not call and gaming or present is ((not call) and gaming) or present. Parentheses say otherwise.
  • The words are lowercase, names are those of the file ([state.<name>], [channel.<name>], [pool.<name>]), and apps, people and auto.
  • A candidate without a condition always holds; below it, the others are never reached, except pools and - below a pool: they get the slots it has no member for.
  • Present means it has something to control: an apps channel while its application plays, an output or input channel while one of its devices is there (always without devices), a person channel while the person is in the voice chat, a homeassistant channel always. A channel stays present absent_after seconds (3 by default) after that ended. apps is present while an application it may take plays, people while someone is in the voice chat, auto while either is, devices while a device no channel has is there, another pool while one of its channels is present.
  • present is only for candidates of slots: a state takes channels with its channels source, and controls apply whatever the slot shows.
  • check-config and the GUI name the mistakes: an unknown state, mode, channel or pool, a word where none fits, a condition that ends too early. The GUI underlines them in the field When.
[slots]
2 = ["browser if present", "auto"]                   # the browser while it plays, else the next application
7 = ["voip if call and not gaming", "auto"]          # the voice chat in a call, but not while gaming
8 = ["game if gaming or present(game)", "-"]         # the game in the mode gaming or while it plays

items.title: Controls and the chord
items.text:
[controls] claims parts of a slot, whatever it shows:

[controls]
2 = { select = { launch = ["mumble"] }, when = "not call" }    # Select starts Mumble while not in a call
5 = { select = "toggle:call", solo = "mode:gaming" }
6 = { fader = "homeassistant", id = "desk" }                    # the fader is number.xtouch_desk_fader

when takes a condition of states and modes: the controls apply while it holds. Actions: homeassistant, cycle_modes, mode:<id>, toggle:<state or mode>, or { launch = [...] } (see Launching the application).

Option of [switching] Default Meaning chord [1, 8] The slots (from 1 on the left) whose Solo buttons, held together, cycle the modes; [] for no chord. chord = { strips = [1, 8], action = "toggle:call" } does another action. banner 1.5 Seconds the LCDs show the label of a new mode, and a slot that shows something else its new label and why; 0 for none.

items.title: Home Assistant
items.text: With [mqtt]: select.xtouch_mode, a binary sensor per state (with since, source and override), an override select per state, an input switch per state with homeassistant = true, binary_sensor.xtouch_<channel>_shown, and sensor.xtouch_slot_<n> (what the slot shows, with label, kind, via and reason). See Home Assistant.

items.title: Channels
items.text:
Each [channel.<id>] section is something a strip of the device can control; slots say which strip shows it when. The id names it in slots, conditions and the entities in Home Assistant: lower case letters, digits and _.

[channel.mic]
type = "input"
label = "Mic"
color = "red"

type picks what the channel controls:

type Page output, input Devices apps Applications person People and the voice chat homeassistant Home Assistant

The strips of auto (the next application that plays) and empty slots (-) are no channels: they are written in the slots.

Options about slots rather than the strip: tags (names to group channels under), in_pool = false (an apps or person channel without a slot stays out of apps, people and auto) and absent_after (seconds the channel stays present after it had nothing to control, for if present).

items.title: Options of every audio channel
items.text:
These options apply to output, input and apps channels, and to auto in a slot. homeassistant channels have only color of them.

Option Default Meaning color "white" The LCD backlight: off (no backlight), red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, white. Dark while the strip has nothing to control, unless lit_when_idle is on. lit_when_idle false Whether the LCD keeps its backlight while the strip has nothing to control: no application of an apps group plays, the device is not there, an auto strip has no application. The fader stays down all the same. meter true Whether this strip's LED meter shows the level (if behavior.meters is on). meter_point behavior.meter_point Where the meter takes the level: "pre_fader" before the volume and Mute of the strip, "post_fader" after them, see Meters. rec "recording" What the LED of the Rec button shows: recording, playing, default, muted or off, see LEDs. solo "off" What the LED of the Solo button shows, the same values, see LEDs. min_volume 0 The volume of the fader at the bottom, 0..200 percent. max_volume behavior.max_volume The volume of the fader at the top, 0..200 percent. encoder depends on the type What the encoder does, see Encoders. fader "volume" "homeassistant" hands the fader to Home Assistant, see Encoders.

Device and application channels also have a label, see their pages. A candidate of a slot can change the look at that place: { show = "mic", color = "blue" } (see Slots).

items.title: Labels
items.text:
A label is the top line of the LCD: at most 7 characters of ASCII, which is what fits. The bottom line shows the volume, or the state of the strip (muted, idle, off).

Where the label comes from:

Strip Label output, input The label of the active profile, else label. Without both: the start of the device's description with device, "Output"/"Input" without it. apps label (required). auto The alias of the application from [aliases], or its name. person label, else the first name of person; people of auto show their name. homeassistant What Home Assistant sets, until then label.

items.title: Volume range
items.text:
The fader covers min_volume at the bottom to max_volume at the top. The encoder stays in that range too. For example, speakers that need amplification:

[channel.desk]
type = "output"
device = "alsa_output.usb-Generic_USB_Audio-00.analog-stereo"
label = "Desk"
min_volume = 50
max_volume = 200
  • Above 100 % the sound server amplifies the audio in software.
  • min_volume must be below max_volume. Without max_volume the top is behavior.max_volume.
  • Profiles and choices of a device can have a range of their own.
  • homeassistant channels have no range: Home Assistant decides what their fader means.

items.title: 100 % at the 0 dB mark
items.text:
The scale next to the faders of the X-Touch Extender marks 0 dB at about 77 % of the travel. The faders of strips that go above 100 % put 100 % there: from the bottom to the mark the fader covers min_volume to 100 %, from the mark to the top 100 % to max_volume. Both parts are linear. behavior.unity_at (default 77) moves the mark.

[behavior]
max_volume = 200   # the top 23 % of the travel amplify by up to 100 %
Fader A linear fader, 0..200 The faders here, 0..200 bottom 0 % 0 % half way 100 % 65 % 0 dB mark (77 %) 154 % 100 % top 200 % 200 %

With the default max_volume = 130 the two parts have the same slope: the fader is linear from 0 % to 130 %, with 100 % at the mark. Strips whose range ends at 100 % (max_volume = 100) are not affected: their 100 % is at the top. The GUI shows the option in "Global settings", "Behavior".

items.title: Elements of a strip
items.text:
Element What it does on an audio strip Fader Sets the volume. Follows changes made elsewhere. Only a touched fader changes the volume. Encoder What encoder says, see Encoders. Mute Toggles mute. Its LED is on while muted. Rec, Solo Their LEDs are indicators. The buttons do nothing, except Rec with profiles. Select On device strips: makes the device the default. On application strips with launch: starts the application. Otherwise nothing on application strips. [controls] can give it another action. LCD Top: the label. Bottom: the volume, or muted, idle, off. The backlight in color, dark while the strip has nothing to control. Ring What the encoder controls. Meter The level of what the strip controls, see Meters.

A strip with nothing to control (a device that is gone, an application that ended) goes dark, and its fader glides slowly to the bottom. When it is back, the fader goes up to its volume again.

items.title: Meters
items.text:
The LED meter shows the peak level of what the strip controls, 10 times a second: from -60 dB (the lowest LED) up to just below full scale (the seventh LED), 5 dB per level of the device (about two levels per LED, see Hardware). A peak at full scale lights the red LED at the top too, for half a second. The device lets a meter fall by itself when no new level comes.

meter_point says where the level is taken, like the pre-fader and post-fader meters of a hardware mixer:

meter_point What the meter shows "pre_fader" (default) The level before the strip's volume and Mute: the meter keeps showing the audio while the fader is down, and the Mute LED says whether it goes on. "post_fader" The level after the volume and Mute: what you hear of an application, what goes out of the output, what applications get from the input. Dark while muted.

What each strip type can show:

Strip "pre_fader" "post_fader" output Before its volume and Mute, as PipeWire's monitor of the output has it. Its monitor times its volume, nothing while muted. apps, auto The streams' audio divided by their volume, so the fader doesn't move the meter. While muted the meter stays dark: PipeWire applies the volume and Mute inside the stream, before anything else can listen, so the audio of a muted stream is gone. The streams as they play. input The input divided by its volume. Dark while muted, as above. The input as applications get it. person, people The voice before the participant's volume (the plugin's fader). Muted, Mumble doesn't fetch their voice: the meter lights while they talk, without a level. A plugin that tells no level before the volume shows the one after it. The voice after their volume, dark while muted. homeassistant The meter entity, see Home Assistant.

The first that sets it wins: the meter_point of the place in a slot, the channel's, then behavior.meter_point.

[behavior]
meter_point = "pre_fader"     # every strip ...

[channel.out]
type = "output"
meter_point = "post_fader"    # ... but this one: what goes out of the speakers

A level divided by the volume is exact while the volume stays. While the fader moves, the audio lags behind its volume by a few hundredths of a second: for 0.3 s after a change the meter divides by the loudest of the volumes since, so a fader pulled down does not light the red LED; the meter shows too low for a moment instead.

items.title: Empty slots
items.text:
[slots]
4 = ["game if gaming", "-"]   # dark while not gaming

- in a slot is a dark strip that does nothing. Its fader stays at the bottom.

items.title: Applications: apps channels and auto
items.text: Application channels and auto control the playback streams of applications, like the per-application sliders in pavucontrol. They need no setup in PipeWire.

items.title: apps channels
items.text:
All playback streams of a group of applications.

Option Default Meaning type required "apps". match required Parts of application names or binaries, ignoring case, or presets like "@browsers". label required The top line of the LCD. encoder "media" media, volume, balance or homeassistant, see Encoders. launch none A command that Select starts while none of the applications runs, see Launching the application. launch_when_running false Select starts launch also while the application runs.

They also have the options of every audio channel: color, meter, rec, solo, min_volume, max_volume, fader.

[channel.voip]
type = "apps"
match = ["@voip"]
label = "VoIP"
color = "white"

A stream belongs to the channel when its application name (application.name) or binary (application.process.binary) contains one of the match entries. "wine" matches wine64-preloader, ".exe" matches Windows games under Proton. xtouch-daemon list-apps shows the names and binaries of the applications that play, and which channel or slot takes each one. A stream can belong to several apps channels.

For common groups there are presets: @browsers, @voip, @games, @steam-games, @music and @video stand for the names of well-known applications of the group, e.g. match = ["@browsers"] for every browser, and mix with names of your own (match = ["@voip", "my-voice-app"]).

Element Function Fader Sets every stream of the group to the same volume. A stream that starts later gets that volume too. Shows the loudest stream. Encoder See Encoders, for all streams. Mute Mutes all streams, or unmutes them when all are muted. The LED is on while all are muted. Select Nothing, or with launch it starts the application. The LED flashes while it starts and is on while it runs, see Launching the application. LCD Top: the label. Bottom: the volume, muted, or idle while no stream of the group is there. Ring What the encoder controls. Meter The level of all streams of the group together.

While no stream of the group is there (e.g. the application was closed), the LCD is dark and shows idle, and the fader glides slowly to the bottom and does nothing. The channel keeps its volume while the daemon runs: when a stream comes back, the fader goes up to it and the stream gets it.

items.title: apps and auto
items.text:
The pool apps is the next application that plays and has no channel of its own, on the slots that show apps. auto is the same, and the people of the voice chat share its slots: people first, from the right, applications from the left (see People). A slot without an entry shows auto.

[pool.apps]
from = "left"                 # the side the applications fill their slots from (also in auto)
hold = 5                      # seconds an application keeps its slot after it stopped playing
exclude = ["notification"]    # never these (by default speech-dispatcher)
color = "cyan"                # the look of every apps slot

[pool.auto]
color = "cyan"                # the look of the applications on every auto slot

[slots]
5 = [{ show = "auto", encoder = "media", max_volume = 100 }]   # the options of one place
6 = ["people", "apps"]        # a person, else an application

The look options of every audio channel go into [pool.apps], [pool.auto] or a place; a place of apps or auto also takes encoder (pick by default: pick, media, volume, balance or homeassistant, see Encoders), min_volume and max_volume. There is no label: the label is the application's alias from [aliases], or its name.

How apps and auto get their applications:

  • An application qualifies while at least one of its streams plays (is not paused).
  • Applications of an apps channel with a slot, and those of exclude, never go to apps or auto; an apps channel without a slot goes in as a whole (in_pool = false keeps it out).
  • Free slots take new applications from the side of from (the left by default), in the order the applications started. A slot that apps has no application for goes to the pool right below it (["apps", "people"]).
  • An application keeps its slot while it plays, and for hold seconds after it stopped. Then the slot is free again. This way a music player does not jump to another strip between two tracks.
  • A newly assigned application keeps its own volume.

With the default encoder = "pick", the encoder chooses the application and a push pins it, so it stays after it stopped playing. See Encoders.

A slot of apps or auto works like an apps channel for its application. Without an application it is dark, blank, and does nothing.

items.title: Launching the application
items.text:
With launch, the Select button of an apps channel starts an application while it does not run: the voice chat, the music player. Any slot can start one with [controls], whatever it shows: 7 = { select = { launch = ["mumble"] }, when = "not call" }.

[channel.voip]
type = "apps"
match = ["@voip"]
label = "VoIP"
color = "yellow"
lit_when_idle = true
launch = ["mumble", "mumble://markus@voice.example.org/Gaming"]
  • launch is the program and its arguments, as a list. It never runs through a shell: no ~, $VARIABLES, pipes or &&. A single string works too (launch = "mumble mumble://markus@voice.example.org/Gaming") and is split like a shell splits it, with quotes, but nothing is expanded.
  • Select starts it only while the application does not run: no stream matches match, and no process whose name contains one of the match entries runs (like processes of states), so a silent voice chat counts as running. For a preset, its processes count, e.g. Steam's reaper for @steam-games. A process named like the program of launch (the file name of its first part, exactly) counts too; that is all a launch of [controls] looks at.
  • While it runs, Select does nothing. With launch_when_running = true Select starts the command also then.
  • The Select LED flashes while the application starts (until it runs, at most 15 s), then it is on while it runs.
  • A second press within 5 s while the application is not up yet does nothing.
  • The application runs on its own: as a transient systemd user service (systemd-run --user, named xtouch-launch-<program>-<random>), so a restart of the daemon does not end it, and its output is in journalctl --user -u 'xtouch-launch-*'. Without a systemd user manager it runs in a session of its own. A program that is not in PATH is a warning in the daemon's log.
  • The process list is read every 2 s.
  • Only the configuration can start programs: neither Home Assistant nor MQTT can, and homeassistant, output, input and person channels have no launch.

items.title: Mumble
items.text:
Mumble connects to a server and joins a channel when it gets a mumble:// URL (Mumble's documentation):

mumble://[username[:password]@]<address>[:port]/[channel[/subchannel...]]
  • The port is 64738 by default. Encode spaces and other special characters of channel names (Gaming%20Night). If the channel can't be joined, Mumble stays in the server's default channel.
  • A running Mumble takes the URL too: the new mumble hands it to the running one and ends. So launch_when_running = true makes Select connect a running Mumble to the server, and launch = ["mumble"] without a URL brings its window to the front.
  • Better leave the password out: the configuration file and the process list would show it. Mumble remembers servers, and certificates need no password.
  • For Mumble as a Flatpak (launch = ["flatpak", "run", "info.mumble.Mumble", "mumble://..."]), keep mumble in match: the program of launch is flatpak then.

items.title: Devices: output and input channels
items.text:
A device channel controls an output (a sink) or an input (a source): one device, one of several, or whatever is the default. With choices, Select switches between several devices, each maybe in a profile of its sound card.

Option Default Meaning type required "output" or "input". device the default device The node name (xtouch-daemon list-devices) or the description of the device, or a list of them; * is a wildcard. Without it, the strip follows whatever device is the default. label see Labels The top line of the LCD. With profiles, the label of the active profile comes first. select true Whether Select makes the device the default. Needs device or choices. choices none The devices Select switches between, each maybe in a profile of its card, see below. Instead of device and profiles. profiles none Profiles of the device's sound card that Rec switches between, see below. encoder "balance" balance or volume, see Encoders.

They also have the options of every audio channel: color, meter, rec, solo, min_volume, max_volume.

[channel.out]
type = "output"
device = "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.analog-stereo"
label = "Speaker"
color = "cyan"

[channel.mic]
type = "input"          # the default input
label = "Mic"
color = "red"

items.title: Elements
items.text:
Element Function Fader Sets the volume, min_volume at the bottom to max_volume at the top. Follows changes made elsewhere. Encoder See Encoders: by default the balance. Mute Toggles mute. The LED is on while the device is muted. Rec With profiles: switches the sound card to the next profile. The LED is on for every profile but the first. Without profiles (also with choices) the LED is an indicator. Solo Its LED is an indicator. Select With device and select: makes the device the default output/input, or switches to the next of several. With choices: the next choice. The LED is on while it is the default. LCD Top: the label. Bottom: the volume, or muted. Ring What the encoder controls. Meter The level: what plays on an output, what an input records.

A device that is not there (e.g. Bluetooth headphones that are switched off) shows off on a dark LCD. Its fader goes down, and the fader and buttons do nothing until it is back.

items.title: The default device
items.text: A strip without device looks up the default device in every state of the sound server. It follows a switch of the default, including its meter. Its Select button does nothing.

items.title: Naming a device
items.text:
xtouch-daemon list-devices lists the node names and descriptions of the outputs and inputs; * marks the defaults.

Use the node name for a device that is both an output and an input under one description, e.g. Bluetooth headphones with a microphone. A description matches only devices of the strip's direction, but a node name is unambiguous and stays the same across restarts.

items.title: Several devices
items.text:
device takes a list, and * wildcards match several devices. Wildcards work on node names and descriptions, and are case-sensitive.

[channel.phones]
type = "output"
device = ["bluez_output.*"]   # whichever Bluetooth headphones are connected
color = "green"

[channel.main]
type = "output"
device = ["alsa_output.usb-Focusrite*", "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.analog-stereo"]
label = "Main"
color = "cyan"

With several devices, the strip shows one of those that are there: the default one, or else the one it showed last. Select makes it the default. Pressed on the default one, it switches to the next one that is there and makes that the default. Without label, the LCD shows which one it is.

items.title: Devices without a channel
items.text:
The built-in pool devices holds the outputs and inputs that no output or input channel has, e.g. a USB headset or Bluetooth speakers. A channel has the devices its device matches; a channel without device has the default device of its direction. A slot that names devices shows the next of them as an output or input strip of that one device: its volume on the fader, Mute, Select makes it the default. auto doesn't take devices.

[slots]
8 = ["devices", "apps"]   # a headset that was plugged in, else an application

[pool.devices]
from = "left"                 # the side the devices fill from (default)
exclude = ["*HDMI*", "alsa_output.pci-*"]   # never a member: node names or descriptions, `*` wildcards
hold = 5                      # seconds a device keeps its slot after it went away (default 5)
color = "cyan"                # the look of the strips of devices, as on an output channel

A device that goes away stays on its slot for hold seconds (its strip shows off), so a short drop of a Bluetooth link doesn't move the strips. present(devices) holds while a device of the pool is there.

items.title: Choices
items.text:
choices is one strip for several devices that are used one at a time, e.g. headphones on the analog output of a sound card, speakers on its digital output, and Bluetooth headphones. Select goes to the next one, and switches the card to the profile it needs first:

[channel.out]
type = "output"
color = "cyan"

[[channel.out.choices]]
label = "Phones"
device = "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.analog-stereo"
card = "alsa_card.pci-0000_11_00.4"
profile = "output:analog-stereo+input:analog-stereo"

[[channel.out.choices]]
label = "Speaker"
device = "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.iec958-stereo"
card = "alsa_card.pci-0000_11_00.4"
profile = "output:iec958-stereo+input:analog-stereo"
max_volume = 200

[[channel.out.choices]]
label = "Buds"
device = "bluez_output.*"

A choice on one line is a TOML inline table: { label = "Buds", device = "bluez_output.*" } in choices = [...]. An inline table can't span several lines, so the [[channel.out.choices]] tables above are easier to read for long ones.

Option Default Meaning device required The node name or description of the device; * and ? are wildcards (the first device that matches). label the start of the description The top line of the LCD while this choice is active (7 characters). card none The sound card whose profile the choice needs: its name or description, wildcards allowed. Only with profile. profile none The name or description of the profile of card the device is in. Only with card. Without both the device is used as it is. min_volume the strip's The volume of the fader at the bottom while this choice is active. max_volume the strip's The volume of the fader at the top while this choice is active, e.g. 200 for weak speakers.

xtouch-daemon list-devices lists the devices, then each sound card (its name, its description and its devices) with its profiles (name and description; * marks the active one): that is where card and profile come from. A device of another profile appears only once the card is in that profile, so write its name as the sound server will call it (usually alsa_output.<card>.<profile output>, e.g. iec958-stereo), or use a wildcard.

  • Which one shows: the choice whose device is the default. If none of them is, the one shown last (if it is still there), or else the first one there is. A choice is there when its device is, or when its card is there and has its profile.
  • Select goes to the next choice that is there, after the one shown, and around. A choice in another profile switches the card first, then its device becomes the default. The label shows the choice at once; if a switch fails, the strip goes back. Pressed again while a switch is on its way, Select goes on from where that one goes, so a few quick presses step through the choices. Pressed on a choice that is shown but isn't the default, it makes that one the default first.
  • The LED of Select is on while the device of the choice is the default. Rec keeps its indicator (rec).
  • Elsewhere: a default chosen elsewhere (pavucontrol, headphones that connect and become the default) shows on the strip if it is one of the choices.
  • Two choices on the same card in the same profile only switch the default.
  • Fader, Mute and the encoder act on the device of the choice shown; its range is the choice's min_volume and max_volume, else the strip's.
  • While none of the choices is there, the strip is dark and shows off; "out if present" in a slot shows something else then.
  • With [mqtt], Home Assistant has a select for the choice.

At least two choices, and not together with device or profiles; select = false does not go with them either. profiles (below) still works, but choices does the same with one button.

items.title: Profiles
items.text:
A sound card has profiles that decide which devices it has, e.g. analog or digital (S/PDIF, IEC958) output. Each profile has a device of its own, so name device with a wildcard that matches all of them. With profiles, Rec switches the card to the next one (see Choices for the same with Select):

[channel.out]
type = "output"
device = "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.*"   # the analog and the digital output of the card
profiles = [
  { label = "Phones", profile = "output:analog-stereo+input:analog-stereo" },
  { label = "Speaker", profile = "output:iec958-stereo+input:analog-stereo", max_volume = 200 },
]
Option Default Meaning label required The name of the strip on the LCD while the card is in this profile, e.g. what is connected to that output (7 characters). profile required The name or the description of the profile. xtouch-daemon list-devices lists the profiles of each card; * marks the active one. min_volume the strip's The volume of the fader at the bottom in this profile. max_volume the strip's The volume of the fader at the top in this profile, e.g. 200 for weak speakers.
  • At least two profiles: one alone has nothing to switch to.
  • The label changes on the press of Rec. In a profile that isn't in the list, the strip's label shows.
  • The Rec LED is on for every profile but the first, so rec can't be set on a strip with profiles.
  • If the old device was the default, the new one becomes the default.
  • Each device has its own volume: the fader moves to the volume of the new one.
  • A card in a profile that isn't in the list switches to the first one.

items.title: People and the voice chat
items.text:
The people of the voice chat come from the provider of [voip] (by default the Mumble plugin). They sit on the slots that show the pool people, and share the slots of auto with the applications: people from the right, in their order, applications from the left (see Where people sit). Someone who should always have a strip of their own gets a person channel.

[pool.people]
from = "right"              # the side they fill their slots from
color = "white"
talking_color = "green"
order = ["Alice", "mum"]    # these first, then the others as they came

[slots]
5 = ["people", "apps"]      # a person, else an application
6 = ["people", "apps"]

[channel.mum]
type = "person"
person = ["Alice", "alice-phone"]   # the same person, from the desk or the phone
label = "Mum"

items.title: The strips of people
items.text:
[pool.people] has the look of the strips of people without a channel of their own, a person channel has the same options:

Option Default Meaning label the first name of person The top line of a person channel; people without a channel show their name. color "white" The backlight while the person is there and does not talk. Dark while they are away. talking_color "green" The backlight while the person talks. meter true Whether the LED meter shows the person's voice. Without levels from the provider it lights while they talk. The level is after their volume, see Meters. max_volume behavior.max_volume The volume of a person with the fader at the top, 1..200 percent; 100 % is at the 0 dB mark as on the other strips. Above 100 % the voice is louder than Mumble plays it, and may clip.

The strips of people have no launch: starting the voice chat is a control of a slot, e.g. 7 = { select = { launch = ["mumble"] }, when = "not call" } in [controls]. A place of people in a slot takes color, meter and meter_point: { show = "people", color = "orange" }.

items.title: Where people sit
items.text:
Option of [pool.people] Default Meaning from "right" The side the people fill their slots from: "right" slot 8 first, "left" slot 1 first. Also inside auto. order none Who sits first: names, or ids of person channels. Then the others in the order the daemon first saw them (it remembers that order for 30 days, across restarts).
  • People sit on the slots whose candidate people or auto wins, in their order. They keep no slot: when someone earlier in the order comes, the others move one slot on.
  • They take the slots where nothing is above them in the stack first, then the others: a slot that a candidate above can take back (voip if call) would move every one of them.
  • A slot people has no one for goes to the pool right below it: ["people", "apps"] shows the next application. A slot of auto takes a person before an application; on ["apps", "people"] the application comes first.
  • More people than slots: the others wait, xtouch-daemon why people says who.
  • "people if call" shows people only while call is on; present(people) holds while anyone of them is in the voice chat. Slots that should never show people say apps instead of auto.

The top line shows the name, the bottom line muted, the volume while the fader moves, or talks. The fader sets the person's volume and Mute mutes them for you, if the provider can. The daemon remembers the volume and the mute it set for each name while it runs, and sets them again when that person comes back (the voice chat starts them at 100 % otherwise). A mute changed in the voice chat itself (Mumble's local mute) replaces the one it set.

items.title: Strips for one person
items.text:
A person channel always shows that person, on the slots that name it. The names are the names in the voice chat, ignoring case, but otherwise exactly (no wildcards, no parts of a name). With several names, the first person of the provider's order with one of them is on the strip.

While the person is not in the channel, the strip shows the name dark, away on the second line and its fader at the bottom; "mum if present" in a slot shows the channel only while they are there. The volume and mute the strip set stay with the name while they are away and come back with them. A person channel without a slot is one of the people (of people and auto) as itself; in_pool = false keeps it out.

items.title: Voice chat
items.text:
[voip] says where the people come from:

Option Default Meaning provider "bridge" bridge: a plugin of the voice chat client sends them (see below). demo: people who are not there and talk in turns, to try the strips of people. participants ["Alice", "Bob", "Carol", "Dave", "Eve"] The names of the demo people.

Without the section, its defaults apply. None of the voice chat clients tells another program the volume of each person, so the daemon can't read them from PipeWire: they all come out of one stream. Mumble and TeamSpeak have plugins that can, and the bridge is what such a plugin talks to. For Mumble there is one: see Mumble, which the GUI installs with a click.

The state voice_chat = true (see States and modes) is on while you are in a channel of the voice chat.

A plugin for another client speaks the bridge protocol.

items.title: Encoders
items.text:
The fader of an audio strip sets the volume, unless it is in Home Assistant. The encoder does what the strip's encoder option says, and its LED ring shows it. After a turn or a push, the second line of the LCD shows the exact value for 2 seconds instead of the volume; moving the fader ends that.

encoder Turn Push Ring LCD volume Changes the volume by behavior.encoder_step per step; the fader follows. Sets behavior.reset_volume. The volume, lit from the left. The volume. balance Moves the balance between left and right, 5 % per step. Nothing for mono devices and streams. Centers it. From the center to the side. L 15%, center, R 5%. pick Picks the application among those without a strip of their own. Pins it. Which of them, as a dot; pinned, lit up to there. Which of how many (2/5); pinned or auto. media Seeks in the track of the applications' media player, 5 s per step. Plays or pauses. How far the track is, lit from the left; blinking while paused, dark while stopped. Where the track is (1:05); playing or paused. homeassistant Changes a number entity in Home Assistant. An event in Home Assistant. The number. The number (42%).

Which channel types have which modes, the default first:

Channel type Encoder modes output, input balance, volume, homeassistant apps media, volume, balance, homeassistant auto (a place in a slot) pick, media, volume, balance, homeassistant

A mode that the type does not have is an error, e.g. channel.web: encoder: pick is not for apps strips (media, volume, balance, homeassistant). With fader = "homeassistant" the default is volume, and it is the only mode. xtouch-daemon check-config shows the encoder of every channel.

homeassistant channels have no encoder option: their encoder is a Home Assistant entity, see Home Assistant.

[channel.out]
type = "output"
label = "Speaker"
encoder = "volume"   # fine steps instead of the balance

[slots]
5 = [{ show = "auto", encoder = "media" }]   # pick is the default for auto

items.title: volume
items.text: Fine steps of the volume. One step is behavior.encoder_step percent (1 by default), and the fader follows. A push sets behavior.reset_volume (100 % by default). Both stay within the volume range of the channel.

items.title: balance
items.text: The balance between the left and the right channel. One step moves it 5 %, so 20 steps go from the center to one side. A push centers it. The ring lights from its center towards the side the balance leans to; only a balance exactly in the center lights the center LED alone, so one a hair off lights the next LED too. The LCD shows the exact balance, e.g. L 15% (the left side 15 % towards the full left), R <1% or center. On mono devices and streams the encoder does nothing.

items.title: pick
items.text:
For auto. Turning the encoder picks the slot's application among those without a channel of their own, paused ones too. One that another auto slot has swaps with it. It works on a slot without an application too.

A push pins the application: it stays on the slot after it stopped playing, until the next push. The ring shows which of the candidates the slot has, as a dot; while pinned, it is lit up to there. The LCD shows which one of how many (2/5) after a turn, and pinned or auto (picked by itself again) after a push.

items.title: media
items.text:
The default for apps channels. The encoder controls the media player of the strip's applications: Spotify, a browser, mpv with mpv-mpris, anything that speaks MPRIS on the session bus. Turning seeks 5 seconds per step, a push plays or pauses. The ring fills up from the left with how far the track is, also while the strip is idle (e.g. paused). It blinks (0.5 s on, 0.5 s off) while the track is paused and is dark while it is stopped, or for live streams without a length. The LCD shows where the track is after a seek (1:05), and what a push made of it (playing, paused).

The player is the one of the process that plays a stream of the strip or of one of its parents, since browsers play from a child process. Without such a player, one named like the application (spotify for Spotify). Playing streams come first. Applications without a player leave the encoder without a function.

A paused player keeps the strip active, also after its streams are gone: browsers end the stream of a paused video a few seconds after the pause, and the strip would go dark with it. It stays lit with its fader at the volume, and the ring blinks; a move of the fader sets the volume the stream gets when it plays again. The strip goes dark when the player is stopped or closed. On a slot of apps or auto this lasts as long as the slot keeps the application (hold of [pool.apps]).

xtouch-daemon needs the D-Bus session bus for this, which a systemd user service has. Without it the daemon logs No media players: the session bus is not reachable (...) once and keeps trying.

items.title: homeassistant
items.text:
The encoder belongs to Home Assistant, the fader still sets the volume. For example, the encoder dims the light next to the speakers. Turning changes number.<ns>_<id>_encoder (0..100) by behavior.encoder_step per step, the ring shows it, the LCD shows the value (42%), and a push sends encoder_pressed/encoder_released on event.<ns>_<id>_buttons. It works while the strip is idle too. An automation in Home Assistant decides what the number does, see Home Assistant.

[channel.desk]
type = "output"
device = "alsa_output.usb-*"  # number.xtouch_desk_encoder
encoder = "homeassistant"

items.title: fader = "homeassistant"
items.text:
The other way round: the fader belongs to Home Assistant (number.<ns>_<id>_fader, with fader_touched and fader_released events), and the encoder sets the volume in fine steps. The LCD still shows the volume. Both need the [mqtt] section.

[channel.music]
type = "apps"
match = ["spotify"]
label = "Music"
fader = "homeassistant"      # number.xtouch_music_fader; encoder: volume

items.title: LEDs
items.text:
Every strip has four buttons with LEDs: Rec, Solo, Mute and Select.

LED On audio strips Mute On while the strip is muted. Select On device strips with device and select: on while the device is the default. Otherwise off. Rec An indicator (option rec). On device strips with profiles it shows the profile instead: on for every profile but the first. Solo An indicator (option solo).

On homeassistant strips every LED is an entity that Home Assistant sets, see Home Assistant.

items.title: Indicators
items.text:
The Rec and Solo LEDs are indicators; their buttons do nothing (except Rec with profiles). Each shows one of:

Indicator Lit while recording An application records: from the input, from the monitor of the output (e.g. a screen recorder), or for apps/auto strips, the application records anything (e.g. Discord using a microphone). Level meters don't count: the daemon's own, pavucontrol's. playing Audio flows: the device runs, or a stream of the applications plays. default The device is the default output/input. Never for applications. muted The strip is muted (like the Mute LED). off Never: the LED stays dark. Option Default rec "recording" solo "off" 
[channel.mic]
type = "input"
label = "Mic"
rec = "recording"   # the default: lit while an application uses the microphone
solo = "default"

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
How the daemon works inside, for developers. To set up the project and run the tests, see Contributing.

graph LR
    Device[X-Touch Extender<br/>/dev/snd/midiC*D0] <-- "raw MIDI (midi.py, protocol.py)" --> Surface
    Surface -- "events: fader, touch, buttons, encoders" --> Desk
    Desk -- "to the controller bound to the strip" --> Mixer[SlotMixer]
    Mixer -- "set_fader, set_text, set_led ..." --> Surface
    Backend[PulseBackend<br/>one pulsectl-asyncio connection] -- "AudioState snapshot after every change" --> Mixer
    Mixer -- "set volume, mute, default" --> Backend
    Engine[SlotEngine<br/>slots/] -- "what each slot shows" --> Mixer
    Backend <--> Sound[pipewire-pulse]
    Desk -- "captures (meter.py), set_meter" --> PwRecord[pw-record, passive]
    Mixer -- "entities of channels, states, slots" --> Bridge[MqttBridge<br/>aiomqtt]
    Bridge <-- "discovery, states, commands, events" --> Broker[MQTT broker / Home Assistant]
    Daemon -- "owns, reloads, stops" --> Surface & Backend & Mixer & Bridge
    Surface -- "what the strips show (live.py)" --> Live[LiveServer<br/>$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/xtouch-daemon.sock]
    Live -- "a JSON line per change" --> GUI[xtouch-daemon gui]
    GUI -- "mode, override, preview" --> Live
    Daemon -- "steps (runtime/slots.py)" --> Engine
    Voip[VoipProvider<br/>voip/] -- "participants" --> Engine & Mixer

items.title: Modules
items.text:
The packages of src/xtouch_daemon/, from the device up. Tests mirror them: tests/<package>/test_<module>.py.

Module Role hardware/protocol.py The Mackie Control codec: decodes the device's MIDI messages into events, builds the messages that drive it. Pure functions. hardware/midi.py Finds the device's sound card in /proc/asound/cards and reads and writes its raw MIDI device without blocking. hardware/strip.py Strip: what a strip of the device shows, sending only what changed; its motor fader glides to its target and stays still while touched. VirtualStrip: a strip that waits off the device. hardware/transport.py How the Surface reaches the device: a Port finds and opens it, AlsaPort the raw MIDI device of its sound card, SocketPort the virtual device's Unix socket. hardware/surface.py Surface: the connection to the device (connects again after it was unplugged), its events, touches, and the startup and shutdown sequences. Shows everything again after a reconnect. Keeps a SimulatedDevice as the mirror of the device (what it sent, what the device reported), which the live view shows. hardware/selftest.py xtouch-daemon test: lights up the device and echoes what happens on it. audio/model.py AudioState: an immutable snapshot of the outputs, inputs, application streams and defaults. audio/backend.py AudioBackend: the interface the strips use (snapshots, volume, mute, default). audio/pulse.py PulseBackend: one connection to the sound server that follows it by events and carries out the commands. audio/meter.py Meter: audio levels from passive pw-record captures. audio/media.py The media players of the session (MPRIS), for encoder = "media". config/ The TOML configuration, validated with pydantic: files (reading it, its errors), model (Config), sections, slots (the channels, states and slots, with the strip of every candidate), the types of the channels' strips (strip, strips, audio_strips, voip_strips), values, names (lists with presets) and presets (@browsers, @steam-games, ..., expanded when the configuration is validated, see Design: presets). strips/ The strip controllers: DeviceStrip (and ChoiceStrip for choices), AppGroupStrip, AutoStrip (the application of an auto slot), VoipStrip (a person), HomeAssistantStrip, EmptyStrip, and the shared VolumeStrip base. A controller gets its Identity (the ids and names of its entities in Home Assistant, its name in the log) and its Look (label, color, meter, LEDs) from outside: the binder makes them per channel and candidate (look_of()). slots/ Design: channels, states and slots without the device: the model (model), conditions (expressions), presence (inputs), the delays (timing), the states and modes (states), the resolver (resolver), the slots over time (simulation), the distinct outcomes (outcomes), recorded observations (recording) and their replay (replay). Pure but for the recorder; the daemon drives it through the SlotEngine, simulate and observe too. mqtt.py MqttBridge: the connection to the MQTT broker for homeassistant channels and controls. Announces their entities (haad-mqtt-autodiscovery), restores the retained states, passes commands on, publishes availability. runtime/daemon.py Daemon: the lifecycle (signals, reload, shutdown, systemd notifications), stepping the slots and the requests for modes and overrides. runtime/desk.py Desk: the strips of the device for as long as the daemon runs. Hands each event to the controller (Presenter) bound to its strip, a release to whoever got the press, follows the hands on the device and the chord of Solo buttons. Its meters (one per strip of the device) capture what the controllers bound now show, so a capture goes on when another slot shows the same. A claim (claim(), the [controls] of a slot) takes the controls it names: their events go to it, and the VirtualStrip of the presenter leaves their fader, ring and LEDs to it (mask()). runtime/controls.py Controls: the [controls] of the slots, built once per configuration with their entities in Home Assistant (number.<ns>_slot_<n>_fader, ..., or the id instead of slot_<n>). After each step the first entry of a slot whose when holds is its claim on the Desk (a slot under a finger keeps its claim until it is let go); it shows what it takes and launches, picks modes (SlotEngine.choose_mode(), cycle_modes()), toggles states and modes (toggle()), or sends events to Home Assistant. runtime/homeassistant.py SlotEntities: with [mqtt], the mode select, a binary sensor, override select and (homeassistant = true) input switch per state, whether each channel is shown, and what each slot shows. Published after each step when they changed (all of them again after the broker was away); choices in Home Assistant go to the SlotEngine, inputs into its observation. runtime/slots.py, runtime/binder.py The slots on the device. config/slots builds and checks the strip of every candidate when the file is loaded; the SlotEngine steps a Simulation 0.1 s after a change (the audio, the voice chat, a finger let go), at the deadlines of its delays and every 2 s for the processes; it takes the requests (a mode, an override, the pick and pin of a slot's pick encoder) and hands out the applications of the auto strips, keeps overrides, the mode picked (slots.json) and the people (people.json) across restarts (runtime/slot_files.py), and carries its state over a reload by id. The SlotMixer (runtime/binder.py) has a controller per channel for as long as the configuration, one per application of auto and per person without a channel while they are members, and an empty one per slot; after each step it binds to the Desk only the slots whose result changed (the others keep their controller, texts, fader and LEDs) and gives a controller the look, encoder and volume range of the candidate it is on. simulator/ The virtual device: device (SimulatedDevice, the model of the device without IO: what the host sets, a hand on it, the motors and meters over time, a broken touch sensor, switching it off and on) and server (it on a Unix socket for virtual-device). The GUI hosts it with Qt (gui/qt/virtual_device.py). See Design: device simulator. system/processes.py The processes that run, from /proc, for the processes of states and launch. system/launch.py Launcher: starts the command of a launch (of a channel or a control) detached from the daemon (a transient systemd user service); LaunchButton: when Select launches, and its LED. See Design: launching applications. system/instance.py The running daemon for other processes: its runtime file (process, configuration file) and where its live view is served. system/systemd.py systemd integration: notify, journal log levels, the unit file, controlling the user service. live/ The live view for the GUI over a Unix socket: messages (snapshots, requests, replies), codec (lines of JSON), server (LiveServer). See Live view. voip/ VoipProvider: the people of a voice chat, with DemoProvider and BridgeProvider (a client plugin on a Unix socket). voip/mumble.py, integrations/mumble/ The Mumble plugin (C): its sources, building its bundle with CMake, finding it and copying it into Mumble's plugin directory. See Mumble. cli/ The command line: one module per topic (daemon, configuration, sound, modes, slots, mumble, service, editor, simulator), put together by main in cli/__init__.py. gui/domain/ The configuration editor without a toolkit: the editable document (slots_document, history, changes), the options of the models (schema), the stacks of the slots (slot_stacks), the look of the strips (looks), suggestions from the sound server (sources), where a problem is shown (problems), applying a saved file (apply). See GUI. gui/qt/ The widgets of xtouch-daemon gui (the gui extra): window/ (the main window, its rail, the window Device, the service, the filter of the keys and the wheel), preview/ (the drawing of the device), pages/ (a module per page; the cards of the page Slots in slot_cards), fields/, theme/.

items.title: Data flow
items.text:
1. PulseBackend subscribes to sink, source, sink input and server events. After a burst of events it takes one snapshot (AudioState) and hands it to the mixer.
  2. The SlotEngine resolves the slots (0.1 s after a change); the SlotMixer binds the slots whose result changed and calls update(state) on every controller. A controller shows the state on its Strip: color, LCD lines, LEDs, ring and fader.
  3. The Surface sends only what changed. A fader target starts a glide that moves the motor every 10 ms.
  4. An event from the device goes from the Surface to the Desk, which hands it to the controller bound to its strip. A controller turns it into commands to the backend. These run as tasks: nothing blocks the event loop.
  5. The sound server reports the result as a new snapshot, which goes through step 2 again.

A homeassistant channel ignores the snapshots. Its entities work as in haad: Home Assistant sends a command, the entity publishes it as its state (retained), and the copy that comes back from the broker changes the entity; the bridge then tells the strip, which shows it. The device's events go the other way: a fader or encoder publishes its number (a fader moved by hand at most every 100 ms), buttons publish events, which are not retained.

items.title: Lifecycle
items.text:
• Start: the daemon starts the surface, the backend and the mixer as tasks and tells systemd READY=1. The device and the sound server do not need to be there: both are connected (again) when they appear.
  • Reload (SIGHUP): the configuration is read again. A file with errors is logged and the current configuration stays. Otherwise a new SlotMixer takes over the same surface and backend and gets the current state right away; the SlotEngine carries its states, picks and people over by id, so slots that show the same keep it. systemd learns about it through RELOADING=1 and READY=1.
  • Preview: a configuration of the GUI (see Live preview) takes over like a reload, from memory instead of the file. A reload ends it: the file runs, or the configuration of the file before when the file can't be used.
  • Stop (SIGTERM, SIGINT): the daemon tells systemd STOPPING=1, closes the mixer, turns every strip dark and moves the faders down, waits for the faders (at most 2 s), sends what is still queued and closes the device. A dark surface shows that nothing drives it anymore.
  • Stop, in this order: first everything stops that could show something (the sound server connection, MQTT, the mixer, the device's events), then the strips are reset, and only then the surface closes. A snapshot that arrived during the reset would otherwise paint the strips again.
  • MQTT: the bridge connects (again) on its own, like the backend. On every connect it publishes the discovery configurations, subscribes, and waits for the retained states with a ping on its own sync topic: the broker sends retained messages before later ones. Entities without a retained state then get their defaults. A reload hands the bridge the entities of the new channels; entities of removed channels are removed from Home Assistant (not by a preview, see Live preview). A changed [mqtt] section needs a restart.
  • Status: systemctl --user status xtouch-daemon shows whether the device, the sound server and (with [mqtt]) the broker are connected.

items.title: Design decisions
items.text:
• One snapshot for all strips. Every strip sees the same consistent state, and one connection serves eight strips. The strips derive everything from the snapshot instead of keeping their own copies.
  • Coalesced volume commands. A fader sends many positions per second. A strip sets only the latest one when the previous command finished, and shows the new value at once, so the display does not lag behind the hand.
  • Passive, native captures for the meters. The meters use pw-record with node.passive = true: a capture never wakes a device, never lights the microphone indicator, and never switches Bluetooth headphones into headset mode. They are native PipeWire streams on purpose: WirePlumber 0.5.18 (PipeWire 1.6.10) restores captures of PulseAudio clients (parec, peak detection streams) at 0 % volume, so those would only get silence. state.restore-props = false keeps WirePlumber from saving the captures at all. node.dont-reconnect = true keeps a capture with its device or stream: WirePlumber makes a stream whose target is the default when it is linked follow the default (like PulseAudio), so without it the meter of the default output would show the next default output after Select. pw-record runs under stdbuf -o0 (coreutils): its buffered output comes in blocks of 4096 bytes (64 ms at 8 kHz), so the meters lagged, and two meters of the same audio differed by up to that much. Unbuffered, it writes every cycle of the graph; the daemon takes the peak of every 20 ms.
  • Meter points from the volume. Measured with PipeWire 1.6.10 (a tone into a null sink, the volume and Mute of the test stream and sink set with pw-cli set-param): a playback stream and an input apply their volume and Mute in their own node, in audioconvert's channel mixer, before their output ports, so every capture of them is after both. audioconvert has monitor ports only on nodes with input ports (outputs, capture streams), not on playback streams or inputs, so there is no tap before the volume to link to; node.passive changes only the scheduling. The monitor of an output is before its volume and Mute (monitorVolumes and monitorMute, both untouched, unless monitor.channel-volumes is on). pipewire-pulse turns a PulseAudio volume v into the linear channel volume v³ (50 % is 0.125). So the meters capture what they can and scale it with the volume the sound server tells (meter.scale_of()): pre-fader divides the audio of a stream or input by v³, post-fader multiplies the monitor of an output by it (0 while muted). The audio of a muted stream or input is gone, its pre-fader level with it. The volume news is ahead of the captured audio, so after a change the division uses the loudest of the volumes of the last 0.3 s (GAIN_SETTLE): a fader pulled down must not light the clip LED. Reference: spa/plugins/audioconvert/audioconvert.c (monitor ports in reconfigure_mode() only for SPA_DIRECTION_INPUT; the monitor volume in impl_node_process()).
  • Stall restart. WirePlumber links a passive capture only once and gives up when that fails, e.g. while Bluetooth headphones disappear and streams move. A capture that gets no audio for 3 s while its device or stream plays is started again.
  • The default device follows by name. A strip without device looks up the default in every snapshot, so it follows a switch of the default device, including its meter.
