  • One owner per strip. A strip belongs to PipeWire or to Home Assistant, chosen by its type. Mixing both on one fader would make two sources fight over the motor.
  • Availability follows the device. The entities are available while the daemon runs and the device is connected, so Home Assistant greys out controls that would do nothing. A last will covers a crash.
  • haad-mqtt-autodiscovery as a path dependency. The entities are the same as haad's, used from a checkout next to this one (like haad does), which also sets the Python version to 3.14.
  • No volume restore in the daemon. The sound server keeps the volumes. The daemon remembers only the volume of an idle application strip, for its next stream, and only while it runs.

items.title: GUI
items.text:
xtouch-daemon gui is an optional editor for the configuration file, in the subpackage gui and the extra of the same name, like the GUI of openhasp-config-manager. The daemon itself does not import it.

  • Toolkit-free domain, thin widgets. gui/domain decides everything: SlotsDocument holds the file as plain values, validates it with parse_config() (the same messages as check-config), and saves it. slot_stacks turns the stacks of the slots into rows to edit, simulate and the outcomes of the slots what other modes and states would show, looks how the live view draws each strip, status whether the device runs the saved file, sources turns sound server snapshots into suggestions, problems which page shows a problem, apply() decides between reload, restart and "the daemon does not run". gui/qt only shows that and passes edits back.
  • Pages by what they edit. A rail on the left of the window Configuration (gui/qt/window/rail.py) has the pages: Slots (a card per slot with its stack, an inspector for the candidate picked, why it shows, Simulate), Channels, States and Settings ([device], [behavior], [aliases], [mqtt] as "Home Assistant", [voip]). Slots, Channels and States are two panes with a PaneSplitter (gui/qt/window/splitter.py) between them, which keeps its share in QSettings.
  • The device on every page. The drawing of the device (DeviceView, gui/qt/window/device_view.py) and the pages with their rail (the window Configuration) are QDockWidgets: one above the other at first, at any side, or windows of their own; QMainWindow.saveState() keeps where they are. The central widget is an empty placeholder, so the docks have all the room. The header and the footer are fixed QToolBars, so they reach across the window and the docks sit between them. A click on a strip of the drawing picks its slot on the page Slots. The menus hold what is used now and then (the theme, the zoom) and the keys of the window.
  • Previews of the controls. gui/domain/demos.py groups the options of a channel by the part of the strip they are about and makes a short scene for each part from the values in the form (frames of a StripState with a caption). PartPreview (gui/qt/preview/part_view.py) shows its steps (‹ and ›) in the same StripView as the window Device, cut to the part; a StripView is drawn in any StripHost. See Design: previews of the controls.
  • Undo instead of questions. History (gui/domain/history.py) keeps the states of the document before every edit, so removing a channel or reverting the file asks nothing and Ctrl+Z brings it back. Typing into one option is one step. Ctrl+Z undoes in the document also while a text field has the focus (gui/qt/window/input_filter.py, which also keeps the wheel from changing a field under the mouse).
  • Forms from the models. gui/domain/schema.py reads the options of every section and channel type from the pydantic models: the type picks the widget (switch, number, choice, color swatches, list chips, masked secret, file), the attribute docstrings become the help, Field constraints the ranges, and Meanings next to a choice (config/values.py, e.g. INDICATORS) say what each value does; Presets on a list of names (StreamNames) makes it suggest the presets of its kind. A new option or channel type needs no GUI code; a test fails for an option without help or a value without a meaning. gui/domain/docs.py holds the "Learn more" links into this site, and a test checks each against the headings of docs/.
  • The comments stay. Saving writes the changes into the TOML document with tomlkit: unchanged values keep their place, their comments and their form (a stack as a string, a list or tables), and a renamed channel keeps its table. The file is written in place, so a symlinked configuration stays one.
  • The daemon is found, not guessed. xtouch-daemon run writes $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/xtouch-daemon.json (its process id, its configuration file, whether systemd started it) while it runs (system/instance.py), so the GUI finds it wherever it was started, and a second daemon names the one that has the device. A saved file is reloaded (SIGHUP) only when the daemon reads that file; a changed [mqtt] needs a restart, since a reload does not take it (another [device] name or virtual it does: Surface.use). The GUI restarts only the service: systemd.Service (shared with install-service) reads the state of the unit, and installs, starts and restarts it.
  • PyQt6, QtAwesome and qt-themes. The same as openhasp-config-manager, so the tools look and work alike. The wheels carry Qt itself, so uv tool install needs no system packages (GTK 4 through PyGObject needs the system libraries and a compiler), Qt paints the strip preview with QPainter and does drag and drop, and pytest-qt runs the widgets offscreen.
  • One visual system. qt/theme/ holds the design tokens: the colors of the dark and the light theme (text at 4.5:1 or more and the outlines of controls at 3:1 or more on every surface, WCAG 2.2 AA, checked by the tests), a 4 px spacing scale, radii, the height of controls and a type scale relative to the desktop font, and the colors of the device for the drawing, the same in both themes. Widgets set style roles (theme.set_role) and take their sizes from the tokens instead of styling themselves. The drawing decides what a strip shows (a StripFace: LCD, ring, LEDs, meter, fader) apart from painting it.
  • One source of truth: the Editor. qt/editor.py holds the document, its history and its validation. Views read from it and change the document only through it, so nothing keeps a copy that could go stale. Its signal changed(Change) comes once per edit, after the document was validated once.
  • Changes say what changed. A Change (gui/domain/changes.py) has a Scope and, for some scopes, a path:
  • VALUE: a value in place; the field that made the change shows it already.
  • CHANNELS, STATES: a channel or state was added, removed, renamed or duplicated.
  • SLOTS: a candidate of a stack was added, removed, moved or changed.
  • SECTION: a section was added or removed.
  • ALIASES: the list of aliases.
  • DOCUMENT: anything (undo, redo, revert).
  • FILE: the file was written, so the document is the same. Each page's show_document(change) updates only what that scope touches.
  • Built once, updated in place. The pages build their widgets once, and showing the document loads the values into them (OptionRow.load()); no page is cleared and built again. A part that comes and goes (a section that is absent, the form of each channel type) is a page of a Stack that is sized to its current part, not a widget that is shown and hidden.
  • No layout for what stays the same. Showing the document again, or a live update 20 times a second, changes no geometry when nothing differs:
  • set_text and the tab texts are set only when they differ.
  • theme.set_role restyles only for another role.
  • The list chips stay while their values are the same. Icons are kept with their name and color (theme.set_icon), so switching the theme draws them again (theme.refresh_icons) without building a page.
  • The options in the order of the device. A channel's form lists its options from top to bottom like its strip:
  • what it controls (device, match, profiles, the id of a Home Assistant strip)
  • the encoder and its ring
  • the LCD
  • the meter
  • the Rec, Solo, Mute and Select buttons
  • the fader and the range of the volume
  • the id This is STRIP_OPTION_ORDER in gui/domain/schema.py, apart from the order of the fields in config/. A test fails for an option without a place in it.

items.title: Live view
items.text:
The GUI shows the strips as the device shows them right now, which only the daemon knows. xtouch-daemon run serves that on the Unix socket $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/xtouch-daemon.sock (mode 0600, next to the runtime file of system/instance.py) for as long as it runs:

  • Whole states, one JSON line each. A client gets the whole state when it connects and again whenever something changed, checked 20 times a second (live.INTERVAL): the LCD lines and backlight, the LEDs, the ring, where the fader is and whether it is touched, the meter level, whether the device, the sound server and the broker are connected, whether the device is the virtual one, and the fingerprint() of the configuration in use. The strips are the Surface's mirror of the device (a SimulatedDevice, see hardware/surface.py): what reached it, with the motors and meters moving as on the device. A line is about 2 KB; a state rather than changes means a client that connects late or misses one needs nothing else. version changes when a line means something else.
  • Requests of the user only. A client may send requests, a line of JSON each: the live preview, a mode and an override (see below). The daemon takes them only from processes of its own user (SO_PEERCRED: root can connect to a socket of mode 0600), and a line of at most MAX_REQUEST (1 MiB): a longer one ends the connection. Otherwise the GUI changes the daemon through the configuration file and a reload.
  • Channels, states and slots. The state has slots (SlotsState): the mode and the one picked by hand, per slot the candidate, channel, pool, member and why, per state its value, since, source and override, and per pool the members that wait. {"request": "mode", "mode": "gaming"} (or auto, "+1") picks a mode, {"request": "override", "state": "call", "value": "on"} (auto, on, off) overrides a state. features has mode and override.
  • A hand from the GUI. {"request": "play", "event": "fader_moved", "strip": 2, "value": 8000} (also fader_touched with touched, button_pressed with button (its note) and pressed, encoder_turned with steps, encoder_pressed with pressed) is taken by the Surface as if the device sent it (Surface.play()), while a device is connected. No answer. features has play.
  • Never in the way. Clients get only non-blocking writes. One that falls behind by more than MAX_BUFFER is dropped (it can connect again), and a socket that can't be made is logged: the daemon runs on without the live view. The server is not one of the parts of the daemon whose end stops it.
  • Applied or not. The fingerprint is a hash of the whole configuration (secrets included). The GUI compares it with the one of the saved file, so it can say whether the daemon took the file, instead of assuming a reload worked (it keeps the old configuration when the new one has errors or a changed [mqtt]).

The GUI reads the socket with a QLocalSocket, without a thread, and connects again while the daemon runs. Without a daemon it shows what the file would show, and says so.

items.title: Live preview
items.text:
The GUI can make the daemon run the configuration in its editor before it is saved (gui/qt/live_preview.py, the daemon side in Daemon.preview()):

  • The whole text, over the live view. StartPreview carries the TOML text the GUI would save (SlotsDocument.render()). The daemon reads it with parse_config(), the parser of the file, so the errors are the same as those of check-config, and runs it like a reload: a new mixer on the same surface, sound server and broker. The file is never written. A text with errors, or a changed [mqtt] (the bridge would need a new connection), is answered with the reason, and what runs keeps running. The GUI sends 300 ms after the last edit, and only a document without problems.
  • Replies the old GUI ignores, features the new one checks. The daemon answers with lines without version ({"reply": "preview", "ok": ..., "message": ...}), which a GUI from before skips like lines of another version. Snapshots tell preview (the daemon runs a preview, and config is its fingerprint) and features (preview, …); a daemon from before tells none and ignores requests, so the GUI keeps the switch off for it.
  • Always back to the file. The preview ends with EndPreview, when the connection of its client ends (the window closed or crashed), without a request for PREVIEW_TIMEOUT (10 s; the GUI sends KeepPreview every 3 s, so a window that hangs with its connection open ends it too), and when the file is loaded: on a reload (saving in the GUI sends one), and when the file changes on disk (checked every second during a preview). The client is told why ({"reply": "ended", ...}). The configuration of the file is kept in memory (Daemon.file_config), so a file that became unusable meanwhile does not keep the preview running.
  • One preview at a time. A second client takes it over, and the first one is told: the window someone works in wins over one that was left open.
  • Visible. The status line of systemd ends with "previewing unsaved changes of the GUI", the log tells when a preview starts and ends and why, and the GUI shows a pill.
  • Home Assistant entities survive a preview. A reload removes the entities of removed channels from Home Assistant (an empty retained discovery message), which also deletes them from its entity registry. A preview doesn't: MqttBridge.set_entities(..., preview=True) only stops driving the entities it does not have, which stay in Home Assistant with their retained states, so the file restores them as they were. The next configuration that is no preview removes what it does not have, like a reload; entities that only a preview had also lose the retained state they left on the broker, so a preview leaves nothing behind.
  • Secrets stay with the user. The text carries the secrets of the file. The GUI sends it only to a daemon of its own user (SO_PEERCRED on its end of the socket), and the runtime directory is the user's own ($XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, or a directory of mode 0700 in the temporary directory).
  • States and modes too. A preview is a whole configuration: the daemon runs it like a reload, carrying the states, overrides and the mode picked over by id, and the mode select in Home Assistant gets the modes of the preview.
  • A situation too. StartPreview may carry a situation (the what-if of Simulate, slots.outcomes.Situation), and its config may be None (the file's). The SlotEngine runs it in a second Simulation (what_if) that starts where the real one is: the states are overrides, the mode is picked, and the sound server and voice chat seen are made for it (Situation.observation: real stand-ins first, made-up ones for the rest). engine.active is what the mixer and the live view use; the real Simulation waits, takes the requests (the chord, Home Assistant, overrides), and is what Home Assistant sees: its slot sensors are not updated during a situation. Nothing of it is written (slots.json, people.json). Snapshots tell simulated; the feature is situation. It ends with the preview. See Design: try changes and situations on the device.

items.title: Channels, states and slots
items.text:
The daemon runs a configuration of channels, states and slots (design).

  • One controller per channel, as long as the configuration. The SlotMixer (runtime/binder.py) builds a controller with its own VirtualStrip for every channel, and one for each application of auto and each person without a channel while they are members. After each step it binds to the Desk only the slots whose result changed: the others keep their controller, texts, fader and LEDs, and their meter capture goes on.
  • The engine decides, the mixer shows. The SlotEngine (runtime/slots.py) is the only one that hands out applications and people; the pick encoder and pins are requests to it (EngineSlot). It keeps the overrides, the mode picked and the order of people in the state directory (slots.json, people.json).
  • Under a finger nothing changes. Slots held on the Desk are fixed inputs of the resolver: a slot keeps what it shows, and its claims, until it is let go.
  • Feedback. A slot that shows something else flashes its label and why for switching.banner seconds; a new mode shows its banner across the LCDs instead.

items.title: Testing
items.text:
The unit tests run without hardware and without a sound server:

  • the protocol codec and the MIDI parser with captured messages,
  • the raw MIDI device against a FIFO,
  • the surface with a recording send, and end to end against the SimulatedDevice in memory (tests/support/simulator.py, on the fake clock of the test) and over its socket,
  • the strips, the mixer and the daemon with a fake AudioBackend,
  • PulseBackend with a fake pulsectl connection,
  • the meters with a fake pw-record script,
  • the MQTT bridge and the homeassistant strips with an in-memory broker (tests/support/mqtt.py): retained messages, subscriptions, last wills, lost connections,
  • the live view with a real Unix socket in a short temporary directory: clients that read, that don't read, and that go away, requests of the user, of other users and that are too long, and the live preview through the daemon,
  • the live preview of the GUI against a fake live view (a QLocalServer) that answers like the daemon,
  • the Mumble plugin built with CMake and loaded into a fake Mumble (integrations/mumble/test/fake_mumble.c), which calls its callbacks as a script says, against a real BridgeProvider (skipped without cmake and a C compiler),
  • the GUI domain with configuration files in a temporary directory and a fake systemctl, and the GUI widgets with pytest-qt on the offscreen platform, with a fake sound server and the dialogs answered by the tests.

The tests mirror the packages of the source (tests/config/, tests/strips/, tests/gui/qt/, ...). Fixtures are in the conftest.py files: tests/conftest.py has the guards every test gets (no processes left behind, nothing of the machine touched, no programs started) and the common fakes, the packages have their own (e.g. the window in tests/gui/qt/conftest.py). What tests import, fakes and helpers, is in tests/support/, never in a conftest.py or another test module.

items.title: Design: channels, states and slots
items.text: Status: decided, being built. It replaces strips, layouts, inherit strips and collapse with concepts that are each edited in one place; the old format goes (see Decisions after the live test). The configuration format may change freely before 0.1.0. Revision 5, after three reviews of the design and a live test of a prototype on the device, see Review log. The resolver and the state engine run in xtouch_daemon.slots and xtouch-daemon simulate; the daemon runs them as a prototype, see Prototype.

items.title: Motivation
items.text:
A [[strip]] today answers four questions at once, and the answers are spread over several mechanisms:

Question Today What does it control? type and its options (device, match, choices, person, ...). When does it matter? Implicitly ("has nothing to control"), collapse, the rules of a [[layout]] (apps, processes). How is it related to other strips? inherit (by layout and position), the voip group, nothing for "these two belong together". Where is it on the device? Its position in a list, shifted by collapse, replaced as a whole by a layout.

That makes simple wishes hard:

  • "VoIP and the Mic only during a call, else auto strips there" needs a group that collapses together, and extra auto strips that fill in. Neither exists.
  • "The VoIP strip matters while gaming and while calling" needs it in two layouts (an inherit strip) and a rule per layout, and the two can't both be active.
  • inherit refers to "strip 6 of the layout default": moving a strip silently changes what the reference means. The author's own configuration shows it: its gaming layout inherits strip 6, an auto strip, where VoIP was meant, and puts Browser where the Mic was, so the Mic is gone while gaming.
  • collapse moves every strip after it: the fader under the finger changes, which hurts muscle memory.
  • The GUI has to show all of it in one strip form, plus a "Layout" tab, plus global pages: it feels unintuitive.

items.title: The model
items.text: Concept Answers Edited on Channel What a strip controls: a device, applications, a person in the voice chat, a Home Assistant strip. Channels page Pool Which one of several a strip takes: whatever plays and has no slot (auto), the next present channel of a list. Channels page People The people in the voice chat: the pool people, and with the applications the pool auto (see people-slots.md). Channels page (look, from and order); the learned order is live there Controls What a fader, encoder or button of a slot does whatever the slot shows (a Home Assistant knob, starting Mumble). Device page State When something matters: a named on/off condition, live, with a manual override. A mode is a state that excludes the other modes (today's layouts). States page Slot Where: one of the 8 strips of the device, with a stack of candidates (channels or pools, each with a condition). Device page

items.title: Names
items.text: Channels, pools, states and the ids of controls share one namespace: an id is lower case letters, digits and _, unique across all four (a control id names Home Assistant entities like a channel id does). auto, people and default are built in. Reserved: and, or, not, if, present, none, mode, and ids starting with state_ or slot_ (they would collide with the entity IDs in Home Assistant). The sigils stay those of today: @name a preset, #name a tag.

items.title: Conditions
items.text:
One expression language says "when" everywhere: in candidates ("mic if call") and in composed states (when = "...").

expr     := or
or       := and ("or" and)*
and      := not ("and" not)*
not      := "not" not | atom
atom     := ID | "present" | "present(" ID ")" | "(" expr ")"
  • ID: a state or mode; default is on while no other mode is.
  • present: the candidate's own channel or pool is present; only in candidates of slots (a state takes channels with its source channels). present(spotify): that channel or pool is. Presence of a pool is defined before slots are assigned (below), so conditions never depend on the result.
  • The GUI shows conditions as chips that read as text: call or gaming.
  • Errors point at the place: slots.7[0]: "voip if cal": unknown state cal (did you mean call?), with a caret in the GUI and check-config.

Conditions depend only on inputs: states and presence. Nothing in a condition depends on what other slots show. That is what makes the resolver deterministic and Simulate truthful.

items.title: Channels: what a strip controls
items.text:
A channel is today's strip without its place: type and the options of that type. The table key is its id.

[channel.out]
type = "output"
color = "cyan"

[[channel.out.choices]]
label = "Phones"
device = "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.analog-stereo"
card = "alsa_card.pci-0000_11_00.4"
profile = "output:analog-stereo+input:analog-stereo"

[[channel.out.choices]]
label = "Speaker"
device = "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.iec958-stereo"
card = "alsa_card.pci-0000_11_00.4"
profile = "output:iec958-stereo+input:analog-stereo"
max_volume = 200

[[channel.out.choices]]
label = "Buds"
device = "bluez_output.*"

[channel.spotify]
type = "apps"
match = ["spotify"]
label = "Spotify"
tags = ["media"]

[channel.alice]
type = "person"
person = ["Alice", "alice-phone"]
label = "Mum"
  • Types: output, input, apps, homeassistant as today, and person (today's voip strip with person, with talking_color, max_volume, meter, launch). Two person channels with a name in common are an error, as today. auto and the group of voip strips are pools; empty is the candidate "-".
  • tags: free-form names for grouping channels, used by pools (#media) and the channels source of states. They are not conditions; name them after what the channels are (media, games), not after states.
  • Presence: whether the channel has something to control: its device is there, an application of the group has a stream, the person is in the voice chat; always for homeassistant. absent_after (default behavior.absent_after, 3 s; today's collapse_hold) delays "absent", so a reconnecting Bluetooth device does not flap; it is present again at once.
  • in_pool (default true, apps and person channels): whether the channel goes into the pools apps and auto (a person channel: people and auto) while it is present and no slot shows it (below).
  • Its Home Assistant entities are named by its id (select.xtouch_out_output), the same wherever and whenever it shows, and they stay available while it is not shown. One owner per stream: the channel, wherever it is.

items.title: Pools: one of several
items.text:
A pool gives each slot that shows it one member that no other slot shows.

Pool Members, in this order apps (built in) Whatever plays and has no slot: apps channels with in_pool that are present and not shown (each as a whole: its label, volume, entities, as in DAW banking), and applications that play and no channel matches. In the order they started playing. A member stays one for hold seconds after it stopped (today's auto_hold). people (built in) The people in the voice chat, see People. auto (built in) Both, sharing its slots; the catch-all. [pool.<id>] channels = [...] The present channels of the list (ids, "#tag") that are not shown by a candidate of their own, in the list's order. 
[pool.auto]
color = "white"
hold = 5                     # today's behavior.auto_hold
exclude = ["speech-dispatcher", "notification"]   # never these: today's behavior.ignore

[pool.media]
channels = ["#media"]
  • The options of [pool.auto] are those of today's auto strips; a pool of channels has none (its members bring their own).
  • Presence of a pool, for if present, counts its members before slots are assigned: auto is present while anything plays that is not excluded, or anyone is in the voice chat (people take its slots; counted before the slots are assigned, so also someone whose person channel has a slot of its own); a pool of channels while one of them is present. Conditions stay independent of the result.
  • Members keep their slot in auto, so applications don't hop around (people keep their order instead). A pool of channels fills by its order instead (the first present channel gets the first slot), which is what collapse does today: Buds coming back takes its place, the others move on.
  • Select does what it does on the member (makes a device the default, launches).
  • Pick (the pick encoder of auto slots), as today: turning picks the slot's member among the applications without a slot (2/5; people are not picked); a push pins it, and it stays on the slot after it stopped playing, until the next push (pinned, auto). A pin beats the pool's order, and people don't take a pinned slot. The resolver keeps the pins: the encoder only asks for one.

items.title: People
items.text:
Decided again on 2026-11-17, see people-slots.md: people is a built-in pool and a candidate, apps the applications alone, and auto both, sharing its slots (people first, each from its side). A pool hands a slot it has no member for to the pool or - right below it (["people", "apps"]), and a slot two pools could fill goes to the one higher in its stack. [pool.people] replaces [people] (from, order, the look), in_pool replaces in_auto, hold and exclude are options of [pool.apps]. What stays from below:

  • The members: everyone in the voice chat who has no person channel, and the person channels (with in_pool, default true) that are present and have no slot of their own, each as itself (its label, look and entities). Like a channel, a person stays a member absent_after after they left, so a reconnect moves nothing.
  • They sit in their order, for muscle memory of who sits where: order (names, or ids of person channels), then the others in the order they were first seen (kept 30 days, across restarts, in ~/.local/state/xtouch-daemon/people.json). Slots where they are the first candidate go first, then the others, each from their side: no block (see people-slots.md). Someone earlier in the order who comes moves those after them one slot on; no slot is kept empty for someone who is away.
  • People don't take a pinned slot. More people than slots wait; there is no paging. Controls of a slot (Controls) don't keep them out.
  • Every configuration has the voice chat's provider ([voip] with its defaults if the file has none), and its socket costs nothing while no voice chat connects.
  • Members are typed: an application, a channel or a person, never told apart by their names (someone called browser is no channel). People are told apart by the voice chat's id of the participant (step 4); order and the learned order go by name.

items.title: States: when something matters
items.text:
A state is a named condition that is on or off, evaluated all the time and visible everywhere: the GUI, the live view, Home Assistant, xtouch-daemon state.

[state.call]
voice_chat = true           # in a channel of the voice chat, also alone (from the bridge)
recording = ["discord", "vesktop"]   # or: one of these records (they open a capture stream only in a call)
delay_off = 5               # stays 5 s after: a reconnect, not much longer

[state.wireless]
devices = ["bluez_output.*"]

[state.focus]
when = "not call and not gaming"

[state.night]
homeassistant = true        # Home Assistant feeds it: switch.xtouch_state_night_input
Source On while apps One of these applications has a playback stream (playing or paused). Names and presets as match. recording One of these applications has a capture stream. Not for Mumble: it keeps its capture stream open while connected, even alone; use voice_chat. voice_chat The voice chat reports that you are in a channel, also alone: joining one says you mean to talk (the mic shows before anyone comes, and the people pool covers who comes). processes A process of one of these names runs (polled every 2 s while any state uses it). devices A device (output or input) that matches is there. channels One of these channels is present: ids, or "#tag". homeassistant Its input switch in Home Assistant (switch.xtouch_state_<id>_input) is on. when The expression holds. Not together with other sources: a state is either composed or has sources.

A state with several sources is on while any of them is. Without sources it is only what its override says. delay_on (default 0) and delay_off (default behavior.state_delay_off, 3 s; for modes 10 s, today's switching.hold, which goes away; 0 for composed states, whose expression has the delays of what it names, so call and not call never overlap) apply to the sources, not to the override. References between states and modes must not form a loop; check-config names it.

items.title: Overrides
items.text:
Every state has an override: auto (the sources decide), on or off. It is set from Home Assistant (select.xtouch_state_<id>), the GUI, the command line (xtouch-daemon state call on) or the chord. One rule for all states and modes:

  • on and off take effect at once, past the delays; back to auto, the sources decide at once too.
  • An override lasts until the sources change (an edge after their delays), then it is auto again. Example: gaming forced off while a game runs (to use the default mode for a moment); when the game exits, auto again, and the next game brings the mode.
  • persist = true keeps it across edges, until it is set to auto by hand. States without sources have no edges, so their override is kept by itself.
  • Overrides are kept across restarts. The first evaluation after a start is the baseline, not an edge: a kept override survives it.
  • An active override shows: hatched in the GUI's state bar, override in Home Assistant's attributes, and in the banner on the LCDs when it is set and when the daemon starts.

items.title: Modes
items.text:
Modes are states with mode = true. Exactly one mode is on: the one with the highest priority whose sources are on (then the first in the file), else default. The override is one select.xtouch_mode with auto and every mode, xtouch-daemon mode gaming, mode --next/--previous, mode --auto. --next and the chord cycle through default and the modes in the order of the file (not through auto). A picked mode lasts until the rules want another mode than before; edges that don't change what the rules want (a mode of lower priority starts) and edges of modes with persist don't end it. A mode keeps label, the banner across the LCDs.

[state.gaming]
mode = true
label = "Gaming"
processes = ["@steam-games"]
apps = ["@games"]

items.title: Slots: where it shows
items.text:
The device has 8 slots, one per physical strip, numbered 1 to 8 from the left. Each slot has a stack of candidates, top first.

[slots]
1 = "out"                   # a single candidate: the same as ["out"]
2 = "browser"
3 = ["game if gaming", "auto"]
7 = ["voip if call", "auto"]
8 = ["mic if call", "auto"]
  • A candidate is "<channel or pool>", optionally with " if <expression>", or "-": deliberately nothing (the slot is dark, today's empty). A slot whose value is a string has that one candidate.
  • A slot without an entry is "auto". A stack whose candidates all don't hold, or lose, ends in an implicit "auto"; "-" at the end makes it dark instead.
  • The table form { show = "...", when = "...", ... } takes options for this place:
  • on any candidate, what it looks like here: label, color, lit_when_idle, rec, solo, meter, meter_point;
  • on an auto candidate also what acts on an application without a channel: encoder (pick, media, volume, balance), min_volume, max_volume.
  • These apply to the applications without a channel the place shows. A channel it shows as a member (an apps channel without a slot) looks and works as the channel; the pool's look only fills in what the channel leaves open. People look as [pool.people] says. What a control does whatever the slot shows (Home Assistant, launch) is in [controls].
4 = [{ show = "auto", encoder = "pick" }]

Two words keep the rules apart: a candidate holds while its condition is true; a slot shows the candidate it gets in the end. Every candidate without a condition holds: a channel that is absent is shown dark (off) and keeps its place, an empty pool is shown dark like an auto strip without an application. "spotify if present" and "auto if present" hold only while there is something.

items.title: The resolver
items.text:
It decides what each slot shows from the inputs (states, presence, pool members, pins, held slots) and, for pool members only, the previous result.

  1. Fixed slots. A slot that is held (a finger, a button) or within its dwell time keeps what it shows; its channel or member is reserved, and the other slots are resolved around it.
  2. Channels by rank. Every other slot proposes its first candidate that holds. A channel that several slots propose goes to the one where it is highest in the stack (its rank), ties to the leftmost slot; the others go on to their next candidate that holds. Repeat until nothing changes. A pool candidate always takes its slot in this step (pools are not contested). It ends: a slot only ever goes down its stack.
  3. Pools. The members are computed now (the auto pool needs to know which channels have a slot) and handed out: the people take the slots of auto from the right, in their order (not pinned ones, see People); pinned members go to their slots; a member of auto keeps the slot it had if that slot still shows the pool and no person took it; the others go to the remaining slots of the pool left to right, in the pool's order (a pool of channels: all by its order). Members left over wait. A slot of a pool without a member for it is dark. The pools of channels go first, then the people take their share of the slots of auto, then auto hands out its applications: a slot meant for a channel gets it before auto takes it as a whole. A pin of a channel that has a slot of its own now is dropped (one channel, one slot).

Pools never fall through and conditions never look at the result, so the steps run once each, in this order: the same inputs give the same result.

check-config warns about candidates that can never show (an earlier one always holds), channels that no stack has, launch channels that only show under conditions, and lists channels in several stacks with the slot that wins each tie.

items.title: Stability
items.text:
• Batching: changes are resolved together 100 ms after the first one (a game starts several streams and a process at once), so faders move once.
  • Dwell: a slot keeps what it shows for at least 1 s before it changes again.
  • Nothing changes under a finger: a held slot is fixed (step 1) until let go. A fader in touchless_faders counts as touched while the user moves it and half a second after, as today; the motor moving it to a new channel doesn't count. The buttons of the chord don't hold slots.
  • Startup: the daemon waits for the first state of the sound server and the first process scan, evaluates the states without delay_on (the baseline), restores the overrides, and only then runs the startup sequence: the first picture is the right one.
  • Reload: the previous result carries over by channel id and pool member.

items.title: Telling what changed
items.text: A slot that changes flashes the new label on the top line and the reason on the bottom line (call, gaming, absent) for switching.banner seconds. A mode change shows its label across all LCDs instead (no flashes per slot at the same time). The motor fader moves to the new volume, as with banking in a DAW. The daemon logs one line per resolution with the changes and the reasons: 7: auto:Spotify -> voip (call: Discord records); Spotify waits.

items.title: Controls
items.text:
What a fader, encoder or button of a slot does whatever the slot shows: actions that belong to the place on the device, not to a channel.

[controls]
4 = { encoder = "homeassistant" }                        # number.xtouch_slot_4_encoder and push events
7 = { select = { launch = ["mumble", "mumble://..."] }, when = "not call" }
1 = { solo = "toggle:night", rec = "homeassistant" }
2 = { fader = "homeassistant", id = "desk_fader" }       # number.xtouch_desk_fader_fader
3 = [                                                    # by mode: the first whose when holds
    { encoder = "homeassistant", id = "strip_3", when = "gaming" },
    { select = { launch = ["obs"] } },
]
  • A slot's controls can claim fader, encoder (turn and push), select, rec and solo; not Mute, which stays with what the slot shows.
  • Actions: "homeassistant" (a number for the fader or encoder, events for the buttons, and a select for their LED), { launch = [...], launch_when_running = ... }, and the actions of the chord: "cycle_modes", "mode:<id>", "toggle:<state>" (the LED shows the state or mode). "toggle:<mode>" picks the mode, and the next press gives it back to the rules (auto); its LED is on while it is the mode. A fader and an encoder only take "homeassistant".
  • A slot has one table of controls or a list of them: the first whose when holds acts, the others don't (a migrated layout per entry). The entries of a slot may share an id; another slot can't have it.
  • A claimed control wins over what the slot shows and owns its LED or ring; the presenter bound there is told which are taken. With the fader taken, the encoder of what the slot shows sets the volume, as with today's fader = "homeassistant"; with only the encoder taken, the fader stays the volume. Under a claimed Select the LED is the launch's. A candidate of the slot can't set the LED (rec, solo) of a claimed button, also while the claim's when doesn't hold: one owner per LED in the file.
  • A channel's own fader/encoder = "homeassistant" (entities by channel id, moving with the channel) stays; a claim of the slot wins over it while it holds.
  • when (states only, no present): while it doesn't hold, the controls go back to what the slot shows. Starting Mumble on slot 7 outside a call leaves VoIP's own Select alone in a call. Nothing changes under a finger: a held slot keeps its claims until it is let go, and a release goes to whoever got the press.
  • Controls don't touch the resolver: they don't hold a slot, people and channels sit there as anywhere. The Solo buttons of the chord can't be claimed.
  • Their entities are *.xtouch_slot_<n>_*, or *.xtouch_<id>_* with id: registered once per configuration, always there, they follow the slot rather than what it shows.

items.title: Pitfalls the design makes possible
items.text:
• Launch: a channel with launch can only be launched while a slot shows it. "voip if call" hides VoIP exactly when you'd press Select to start the voice chat: put the launch into [controls] with when = "not call". check-config warns.
  • Indicators: a hidden channel's LEDs are not on the device. mic if call hides the Mic and its Rec LED, which lights while any application records (a meeting in a browser tab, OBS).
  • A voice chat without room: people in a Mumble call while no auto slot is free for them wait; the why line says so ("Bob waits").

items.title: Home Assistant
items.text: Entity What The entities of a channel (number.xtouch_<id>_fader, select.xtouch_<id>_output, ...) As today's strips, named by the channel id, registered once per configuration: they stay available (and keep their state) while the channel is not shown or moves to another slot; the buttons of a homeassistant channel send events only while it is shown. The entities of the controls of a slot (number.xtouch_slot_<n>_fader, event.xtouch_slot_<n>_buttons, ..., or <id> instead of slot_<n>) Registered once per configuration, always there, whatever the slot shows. binary_sensor.xtouch_<id>_shown Whether the channel is on a slot. sensor.xtouch_slot_<n> What slot n shows: a channel id (also one auto hands out), app:<application>, person:<name>, or none. Attributes label, kind (channel, app, person, none), via (the candidate: a channel or pool id), reason. binary_sensor.xtouch_state_<id> The state. Attributes since, source (which source turned it on), override. select.xtouch_state_<id> The override: auto, on, off. switch.xtouch_state_<id>_input Only for homeassistant = true: what Home Assistant feeds into the state. select.xtouch_mode The mode override: auto and every mode. Replaces select.xtouch_layout.

items.title: The chord
items.text: [switching] chord = { strips = [1, 8], action = "cycle_modes" } (default). action = "toggle:call" toggles the override of a state instead (auto -> the opposite of its value now -> auto). The same actions are those of buttons in [controls]; the Solo buttons of the chord can't be claimed there.

items.title: A complete example
items.text:
The author's configuration in this format (today about 110 lines):

# [device], [behavior], [aliases], [mqtt] unchanged

[channel.out]
type = "output"
color = "cyan"
choices = [ ... ]   # the three choices above

[channel.browser]
type = "apps"
match = ["@browsers"]
label = "Browser"
color = "blue"
meter = true

[channel.game]
type = "apps"
match = ["@games"]
label = "Game"

[channel.voip]
type = "apps"
match = ["@voip"]
label = "VoIP"
color = "yellow"
lit_when_idle = true
in_pool = false             # notification sounds of Discord don't take an auto slot

[channel.mic]
type = "input"
device = "alsa_input.pci-0000_11_00.4.analog-stereo"
label = "Mic"
color = "red"
encoder = "balance"

[pool.auto]
color = "white"

[pool.people]               # they take auto slots from the right (next to VoIP), applications from the left
color = "yellow"

[state.gaming]
mode = true
label = "Gaming"
processes = ["@steam-games"]
apps = ["@games"]

[state.call]
voice_chat = true
recording = ["discord", "vesktop"]
delay_on = 0               # voice_chat and recording have no blips to swallow
delay_off = 5               # VoIP and Mic stay through a reconnect, not much longer

[slots]
1 = "out"                       # always the speaker/phones/buds
2 = "browser"
3 = ["game if gaming", "auto"]  # the game next to the browser
4 = [{ show = "auto", rec = "recording" }]
7 = ["voip if call", "auto"]
8 = ["mic if call", "auto"]

What it shows, as xtouch-daemon simulate docs/development/design/channels-states-slots.toml --table prints it (the example is that file; a test keeps this table in line with it): one row per combination of states and presence the stacks ask about that changes something.

when             1    2        3     4-6   7     8
default          out  browser  auto  auto  auto  auto
call             out  browser  auto  auto  voip  mic
gaming           out  browser  game  auto  auto  auto
gaming and call  out  browser  game  auto  voip  mic
  • People share the auto slots: they sit as a block from the right, next to VoIP, in their order (order, then the order they were first seen in); applications fill the auto slots from the left. A person takes the slot of an application only if no auto slot is free, and the application moves to a free one or waits.
  • With Mumble, joining a channel turns call on at once (delay_on = 0): VoIP, Mic and the person show up together. Leaving shows at once on the person's strip; VoIP and Mic stay 5 s, through a reconnect.
  • A candidate can set options of its strip: slot 4 sets rec (here to its default, the REC LED shows recording).

  • Device (the start page):
  • The state bar is live and read-only: each state with its value and since when. Its ▾ menu sets the override (auto, on, off), which changes the daemon; an overridden state is hatched, with ⟲ to go back to auto.
  • The live device stays as today (LCDs, meters, faders, the buttons), above the stacks.
  • Simulate is a separate mode, named so it can't be mixed up with the existing Live preview (which runs the unsaved file on the device). It draws a colored frame around the device and opens a bar of what-if inputs: every state, the presence of the channels and pools the stacks ask about, and how many members each pool has. The device then shows what the resolver would. Nothing is sent. Esc ends it.
  • Each slot is a card with its stack: one row per candidate with its condition as text chips (call or gaming, always), ▶ on the one shown. Drag and drop or Ctrl+Up/Down reorder; "+ add" or dropping a channel or pool adds a candidate, and its condition opens as chips right away (in Simulate, prefilled with the states turned on).
  • The why line tells for the selected slot what it shows and why not the candidates above it, from the resolver's trace; for a selected channel where it is and why not elsewhere (Browser: on 2; not 8 (tie to 2)). The same is xtouch-daemon why 2 and xtouch-daemon why browser.
  • The inspector edits the candidate (condition as chips or as text, the options for this place) and its channel or pool in one panel; it says where else that channel is used. Below the card, the slot's controls: per fader, encoder and button what it does whatever the slot shows, with their when.
  • Grid shows the distinct outcomes, as in the example above. Clicking a row simulates it, clicking a cell selects that card.
  • Channels: channels and pools, people with its look, order, and the learned order live, to drag into order) in a list with type icon, label, tags and where they are used. The inspector is today's strip form without place and layout. "Duplicate" replaces copy and paste of strips.
  • States: modes first, then the other states: sources or composition, delays, live value with since when and which source, override, and which stacks use it.
  • Settings: [device], [behavior], [aliases], [mqtt], [voip], [switching].

Undo, validation, the Live preview and the problem list stay; problems link to a slot, candidate, channel, pool or state. The GUI keeps the form a stack has in the file (string, compact list or tables) and its comments.

items.title: The daemon
items.text:
Slots replace strips and layouts in the daemon (no translation into today's strips): what lives as long as the daemon, the configuration or a member, and a binder that changes only the slots whose result changed.

Part Lives as long as What Desk (runtime/desk.py) the daemon The 8 strips of the device: the touch, buttons and touchless faders (held_slots()), the events to the presenter bound to each slot, the meters of the bound presenters, banners and flashes. Replaces Mixer and Flow. SlotEngine (runtime/slots.py) the daemon The StateEngine, presence, the members of the pools, the resolver with dwell, pins and the order of the people; keeps overrides, the mode pick and the people across restarts; wakes at the deadlines of the delays (no polling). A reload carries the run state over by state, channel and member id. Replaces SlotRunner and LayoutSwitcher. ChannelSet (runtime/channels.py) the configuration (diffed by id on reload) One controller per channel, with its own VirtualStrip, and its entities, registered once. Members (runtime/members.py) a member A controller per application of auto (today's AutoStrip without AutoSlot) and per person (today's voip strip with a participant id, without VoipSeats): made when it becomes a member, closed when its hold or absent_after ends; it moves between slots unchanged. Places (runtime/places.py) the configuration The options of auto candidates: their look, and what acts on the application without a channel they show (the pick, media, volume, balance encoder, the volume range). Controls (runtime/controls.py) the configuration The [controls] of each slot with their entities: bound to the Desk's slot, not to what it shows; they take the claimed controls from the presenter while when holds. Binder (runtime/binder.py) the daemon Compares a result with the one before and binds only the slots that changed (VirtualStrip.bind); unbinds what is no longer shown; the flashes and their reason. A controller gets its look (label, color, lit_when_idle, rec, solo, meter, meter_point) when it is bound, its identity is its channel or member. Home Assistant (runtime/homeassistant.py) the configuration The entities of states, overrides, the mode and the slots. Live view A snapshot of the slots (per slot the candidate, channel, pool, member and why), the states (value, since, source, override), the mode and who waits; requests SetMode and SetOverride.
  • Goes away: Mixer, placement.py, layouts.py, AutoAssigner/AutoSlot, VoipSeats, Shape/DARK/showing, config/strips (the [[strip]] types), the layouts, inheritance, and handing the applications of apps channels to behavior.ignore.
  • The resolver alone decides which member shows where; the encoder's pick and pins are requests to the SlotEngine.
  • Times come from the loop's clock (loop.time()).
  • check-config prints channels, pools, people, states with their sources, per slot its stack, the outcome table, and the warnings above. list-apps says per application which channel, pool or slot has it.

items.title: The order of the work
items.text:
Each step keeps the daemon working and the tests green:

  1. The format: [people], no people candidate (both revised in people-slots.md), people skip pins, person channels in the block, the presence of auto, typed members, [controls] (read and checked; they run from step 5c on), talking_color only for people.
  2. Desk out of Mixer, for both formats: touch and held buttons survive a new mixer. See Step 2.
  3. Controllers get their look, identity and entity ids from outside (the old format from its strips).
  4. SlotEngine with pins, overrides and persistence, carried over a reload; the prototype takes the applications of auto from the result. Pins hold a typed member (application or channel, like Person), people go by the participant's id.
  5. The slots natively: ChannelSet, Members, Places, Controls, Binder on the Desk; Shape and the rebuilding go; entities per channel and per slot's controls.
  6. Home Assistant: states, overrides, the mode (replaces the layout select), the slots. The chord gets its new form, and its check against [controls] moves into Scene.of() (now in config/slots.py).
  7. The live view: the snapshot and requests above; the GUI shows them read-only.
  8. check-config, init-config, the docs. migrate-config was not built: the old format is a clean break, an old file fails check-config.
  9. The old format and its runtime go.
  10. The GUI edits the new format.

items.title: Step 2: the Desk
items.text:
• Presenter: what the Desk calls of a controller (today's StripController): strip, the on_* handlers, meter_targets, is_playing, target_gain, held_meter, close, and taken_controls (step 5).
  • The Desk API: bind(slot, presenter | None, meter_point), held_slots() (slots from 1), dispatch(event). A presenter bound to a slot a finger is on gets on_touch(True) at once, so it knows (in the old format a layout switch rebinds under a finger; in the new one a held slot doesn't change).
  • dispatch routes by slot and control (fader, encoder, each button) to an owner: the bound presenter, or a claim (a hook that stays empty until step 5 brings [controls]). It is sticky: a release (button up, encoder push up) goes to whoever got the press, even if bind() changed in between. A touched fader goes over instead: on bind() the presenter that had it gets on_touch(False), the new one on_touch(True), its moves and its release, so each sees a touch and its release.
  • Until step 9 the old format binds the controllers of its mixer through the Flow (strip_at).
  • The Desk owns the meters from step 2 on: it runs the meter loop for the presenters bound now.
  • The Desk also keeps the chord's held Solo buttons and the flashes and banners of the slots.
  • The GUI's live preview uses the same Desk: touch and held buttons carry over its start and end.
  • Tests: tests/runtime/test_desk.py with what moves from test_mixer.py, and "a finger on fader 2 during a change of slot 7 keeps slot 2 as it is, and the new presenter of slot 2 knows about the finger".

items.title: Step 9: the old format goes
items.text:
Decided 2026-11-17: step 9 before step 10; the GUI may not edit configurations in between.

  • 9a, reading: the old Config (strips, layouts and their checks), LayoutConfig, InheritStripConfig, Inheritance and the old-only options (behavior.auto_hold, ignore, collapse_hold, switching.hold) move to config/legacy/ (the GUI read it until step 10; it is gone now). parse_config refuses a file with [[strip]] or [[layout]]; a file without [slots] is one of channels, states and slots with all slots auto, so Config.slots is always there. The defaults without a file are config.example.toml.
  • 9b, runtime: the daemon runs only slots: Mixer, runtime/layouts.py (LayoutSwitcher, layout_file), placement.py, AutoAssigner/AutoSlot, VoipSeats, collapse in the strips, select.<ns>_layout, and in the live view layout, layouts, placement and SwitchLayout go; xtouch-daemon layout fails with a pointer to mode. The binder reads hold and the excluded applications from the scene, not from [behavior].
  • 9c, commands: check-config describes channels, states and slots (the table, and per channel what it is), list-apps says which channel, pool or slot takes each application, test and run as before.
  • 9d, docs: the pages of strips, layouts and collapsing go into Channels, states and slots; Getting started, Home Assistant, Commands, Architecture and the example follow.

items.title: Step 10: the GUI edits the new format
items.text:
Decided 2026-11-17: the whole of The GUI, in these commits:

  • 10a, the document: gui/domain/slots_document.py, the file as plain data with option paths (("channel", "mic", "label"), ("slots", "3"), ("state", "call", "delay_off")), written back into the TOML text with its comments and the form of each stack. An old file fails to open with the errors of check-config. validate() runs parse_config() and gives each problem its path. Undo as today.
  • 10b, the rail, Settings and Channels: a left rail (Device, Channels, States, Settings); Settings are today's section pages; Channels lists channels and the pools (apps, people, auto and those of channels) with type, label, tags and where they are used, the inspector is today's strip form, with Add, Duplicate and Remove.
  • 10c, States: modes first, then the other states: sources or when, delays, persist, live value since when and from which source, the override, and which stacks use it.
  • 10d, Device: the live device with the state bar (live, override menus) above slot cards: each stack as rows with their conditions as chips, ▶ on the one shown, add, remove, Ctrl+Up/Down and drag and drop; the inspector edits the candidate (show, condition as chips or text, place options) and its channel, and says where else the channel is used; below it the controls of the slot.
  • 10e, why: the why line from the resolver's trace for a slot or a channel, and xtouch-daemon why <slot or channel>.
  • 10f, Simulate and Grid: Simulate (a frame around the device, a bar of what-if inputs, the device shows what the resolver would, nothing is sent, Esc ends it) and the Grid of distinct outcomes (a row simulates it, a cell selects its card).
  • 10g, the old GUI goes: strips and layouts in the GUI, config/legacy, the old example and init-config --strips, layout, layouts, placement and SwitchLayout of the live view; the GUI page and its screenshot follow.

items.title: Migration
items.text:
Not built (decided 2026-11-17: a clean break). An old file fails check-config; this is how to write it anew:

Old New A strip A channel and a candidate in the slot of its position. Its id: its id; for a strip with Home Assistant entities strip_<position> (so select.xtouch_strip_1_output keeps working), with a suggestion to rename it; else its label in lower case, else <type>_<n>. homeassistant strips that share entities across layouts One channel. An auto strip auto; its options that differ from those of the other auto strips become options of the place. Candidates the same as the slot's fallback are dropped. A voip strip Without person: a people candidate, its look goes to [pool.people]; people fill slots from the right in their order, so their strips move; label and paging go. With person: a person channel. A launch goes to [controls] of its slot, select = { launch = ... } (decision 6). fader/encoder = "homeassistant" and launch of an auto strip [controls] of its slot, with id = "strip_<n>" so the entities keep their ids. An empty strip "-". A [[layout]] A [state.<name>] mode = true with its rules, label and priority; each of its strips a candidate if <name> above the default one of that slot. meter_point of a layout meter_point on the places of its candidates. An inherit strip A candidate of the channel it refers to. The report names every one it resolved, so surprises (like the one in the motivation) show. collapse on a strip The strip stays in its slot as "<id> if present" above auto: nothing shifts any more. The report lists them and points to pools of channels for those who want filling by order. behavior.auto_hold, behavior.ignore [pool.apps] hold, exclude. behavior.collapse_hold behavior.absent_after. switching.hold delay_off of each mode. switching.chord = [1, 8] chord = { strips = [1, 8], action = "cycle_modes" }. The remembered layout (layout_file) The kept override of the mode. Strips with the same strip_<n> entities in several layouts that control different things Separate channels; the report names the entities that are renamed. select.xtouch_layout, xtouch-daemon layout select.xtouch_mode, xtouch-daemon mode; the old command fails with a pointer, the report names the entity for automations.

No compatibility reading of the old format.

items.title: Tests the design needs
items.text:
The resolver and the state engine are pure, so each rule gets unit tests, among them every scenario the reviews traced:

  • the example's table, row by row, and joining Mumble while gaming (VoIP, Mic and the person at once);
  • a channel several stacks want at the same and at different ranks; an exhausted stack ending in auto; "-";
  • a held slot keeping a channel another slot now ranks higher; a touchless fader moved by the user and by the motor;
  • pool members keeping their slots and waiting (6 applications, then a call); pick and pins; people in their order from the right, moving applications only when needed; a pool of channels filling by order; a hidden channel taking an auto slot as a whole, and in_pool = false;
  • batching and dwell; startup as the baseline with a kept override; a reload carrying the result over;
  • delay_on swallowing a join tone; overrides in all three values, ending at an edge, with persist;
  • modes by priority, the mode override with auto, --next order, default in conditions;
  • composed states, loops, reserved and duplicate names, errors with positions;
  • an absent channel holding versus if present, absent_after, presence of pools.

items.title: Prototype
items.text:
Three reviews of prose found three rounds of holes, each in the parts that only existed as prose. So the resolver and the state engine are code now, pure (no sound server, no device), in xtouch_daemon.slots:

Module What model Scene.of(): reads [channel.*], [pool.*], [state.*], [slots] with every check above. expressions The conditions, with errors at their position. inputs, timing An Observation (applications, voice chat, processes, devices, Home Assistant), presence, the delays. states StateEngine: sources, delays, overrides, modes, composed states, the baseline. resolver resolve(): fixed slots, channels by rank, pools; the trace. simulation Simulation: all of it over time, with the dwell time and held slots. outcomes The distinct outcomes: the table above, simulate --table, the GUI's grid. recording, replay observe records the real system; simulate --replay replays it: changes, flaps, time on.

xtouch-daemon simulate docs/development/design/channels-states-slots.toml --mode gaming --state call --playing firefox shows the slots and why. The tests (tests/slots/) have the scenarios the reviews traced that the prototype covers, and one keeps the table above in line with the example. Not in the prototype: batching (a matter of when the daemon calls it), the touch sensors (their result is held), reload carrying the result over, cycling through modes (--next), Home Assistant and the live view, the GUI, the migration.

What building it showed:

  • An override set while a delay is pending ends with it. call forced off while a join tone's delay_on runs: 2 s later the sources turn on (an edge), the override ends, and the call comes anyway. That is the rule ("until the sources change"); whether it is what people expect needs trying on the device.
  • The grid explains rank surprises. A test configuration with 1 = ["buds if present", "out"] and 3 = ["out if video", "auto"]: in video mode without buds, out goes to slot 3 (rank 1 there, 2 on slot 1), and slot 1 shows auto. Correct, but only the grid (or check-config's list of shared channels) makes it visible.
  • present on "-" meant nothing: now an error.
  • Channels of a pool without a slot don't wait: only applications and people do; such channels are just not shown.
  • A multi-line inline table is no TOML 1.0: the examples of choices use [[channel.out.choices]].
  • The code review (a DAW, Linux desktop and Home Assistant user, reviewing the code with counter-examples) found seven bugs no scenario had caught, all fixed with a test each: a held slot didn't reserve a channel it showed in auto, nor did pins check for one, so a channel could be on two slots; auto took a channel before the pool of channels meant for it; pool members had no delay (a Mumble reconnect moved a fader twice) and hold wasn't used; persist didn't apply to modes, and any mode edge ended a pick; replays missed flaps after long stable times. Also: present in a state's when is an error now, composed states have no delays of their own, simulate checks its options, and --table no longer shows composed states apart from what they name.

On the device: the daemon runs a file in this format (xtouch-daemon run -c slots.toml). The resolver runs every 0.2 s (that is the batching) on what the sound server, the processes and the voice chat of the daemon show. Each channel has its controller for as long as the configuration, each application of auto and each person without a channel one while they are members (SlotMixer in runtime/binder.py, step 5b); after each step only the slots whose result changed get another controller, so the others keep their texts, fader and LEDs; a slot that shows another candidate flashes its label and why (the when of the new candidate, or not <when> of the old one) for switching.banner seconds, unless the mode changed (its banner says it). [controls] run (runtime/controls.py, step 5c): the first entry of a slot whose when holds claims its controls on the Desk, shows their fader, ring and LEDs, and launches, picks modes, toggles states or puts them into Home Assistant. Apps channels never go into auto one application at a time, only as a whole. The mode takes the place of the layout: xtouch-daemon layout gaming, the GUI and the chord pick a mode, layout auto gives it back to the rules; the banner names a new mode. With [mqtt], Home Assistant has the entities of Home Assistant (runtime/homeassistant.py, step 6). Not yet: the GUI (it can't edit the format).

Next: see Decisions after the live test.

items.title: Decisions after the live test
items.text:
The prototype ran on the author's device (the example above). Decided then:

  1. People only share auto (revised 2026-11-17 in people-slots.md: people, apps and auto are built-in pools). people is no candidate of a slot any more, and share goes: people always take auto slots from the right, in their order. One way to place people; no paging. Fixed people are person channels.
  2. Slots replace strips and layouts in the daemon. Not a translation into today's strips: channel controllers that live as long as the configuration, bound to slots by the resolver (The daemon).
  3. The conditions stay as they are ("x if y" strings with the grammar above): they read well and worked on the device.
  4. One format. The old one goes: no reading of it, and no migrate-config either (Migration). The GUI, the docs and init-config move to the new format.
  5. person channels without a slot join the people as themselves (in_pool to opt out), like apps channels join auto.
  6. Starting the voice chat is a control of the slot VoIP shows on: 7 = { select = { launch = [...] }, when = "not call" } in [controls]; the VoIP channel stays hidden outside a call, the strips of people have no launch.
  7. [people], not [pool.people]: people are no pool any more (revised 2026-11-17: [pool.people]).
  8. [controls]: actions that belong to a slot, whatever it shows (Controls). Options of places only look, or act on applications without a channel.

Found on the device and changed in the prototype: call on at once and off after 5 s (a delay showed VoIP and Mic after the people, a long one hid leaving); people in a learned order instead of fixed home slots (no empty slots); people from the right, applications from the left (they don't push each other around); voice_chat also alone (the mic before anyone comes); the meters of people on the dB scale like every other meter.

items.title: Sixth review (the integration of the fifth)
items.text: Finding Decision A pinned member a held slot shows went to its pin's slot too: one stream on two strips. A pin waits while a held slot shows its member. Claims could change under a finger; a release could go to another owner than the press. Held slots keep their claims; dispatch is sticky and routes by control. Minor: untyped pins and members by display name; an id on controls without Home Assistant; an empty launch; launch_when_running in [people]; LEDs of claimed buttons with a when; the chord check outside the model; two homes for Home Assistant faders; LEDs under claims. Step 4; errors; refused; one owner per LED; step 6; both stay, the slot's claim wins; stated. bind() lacked the meter point the Desk needs for its meters. bind(slot, presenter, meter_point). Owner: one table of controls per slot can't change with the mode (layouts with different controls on a strip). A list per slot, the first whose when holds. Owner: toggle:<mode> had no meaning (modes have no override of their own). Picks the mode, the next press back to auto.

items.title: Fifth review (the integration of the fourth, and actions of places)
items.text: Finding Decision Actions (a Home Assistant knob, a launch) only worked through what the slot showed: a channel or a person there silently disabled them. [controls] per slot (decision 8). Blocker: participant names and channel ids were one namespace of members: someone called browser became the Browser channel and broke the strips. Typed members (application, channel, person). Options that kept people off a place disagreed between code and design; place ids couldn't be reused; decision 6 hung on people skipping places. Gone with [controls]: only pins keep people out. Minor: launch in [people]; a [voip] provider in every configuration; auto present for people who never sit in it; a dropped pin kept people out; the table doesn't explore people; participant ids. Refused; said in the design (people share auto everywhere, the bridge socket costs nothing without a voice chat); fixed; fixed; Simulate gets a count of people (step 7); step 4.
