items.title: Fourth review (architecture, after the live test)
items.text: Finding Decision Blocker: entities were named by strip (strip_<n>) and went away with a channel's slot; place options overrode a channel's controls and id. Entities per channel and place id, registered once per configuration; place ids in the namespace; place options only for applications without a channel. Blocker: the mixer handed out the applications of auto itself, in its own order, next to the resolver; pins never reached the resolver. The resolver alone; pick and pins are requests to the SlotEngine. Touch and held buttons died with each new mixer. The Desk lives as long as the daemon. People on places with controls, people and pins. People skip pinned slots and places with control options; pick only lists applications. The presence of auto didn't count people. It does. person channels without a slot vanished. They join the people (decision 5). Leftovers of share and the people candidate. Gone; [people]. A reload lost the run state. The SlotEngine outlives the configuration. Controllers had their place built in; the live view counted strips by layout. Look and identity when bound; a snapshot of slots and states. The voice chat's launch had no home. A launch on the place VoIP leaves (decision 6). Minor: clocks, people by name, sensor.xtouch_slot_<n>, migration rows, polling, entity churn of the prototype. loop.time(), ids for members, the sensor's format, the rows, deadlines; the native runtime ends the churn.

items.title: First review (DAW, Linux desktop and Home Assistant user)
items.text: Finding Decision voip was both a channel and the built-in pool. Pools became a concept; one namespace and the pool people. An off-delay without an on-delay: a notification sound turns call on for 30 s. delay_on/delay_off; recording and voice_chat as sources. "Leftmost wins" ranks by position. Rank first, ties to the left. Too many ways to say "when". One expression language; tags only group channels; when is exclusive with sources. Modes and states were two concepts with two syntaxes. mode = true on a state; every state has an override. present was undefined for absent channels. An absent channel holds (dark, keeps its place); if present skips it. A touchless fader can't protect "nothing under a finger". It counts as touched after the user moved it. No feedback when a slot swaps. The new label plus the reason. Home Assistant needs to know what shows where. sensor.xtouch_slot_<n>, binary_sensor.xtouch_<id>_shown. Long syntax. [channel.<id>], the compact slot form. GUI: preview and override looked the same; no overview. Read-only state bar with override menu, Simulate, chips, one inspector, the why line, the grid. Migration breaks strip_<n> entities. Kept where entities exist, with a rename suggestion.

items.title: Second review (DAW, Linux desktop, Home Assistant user, systems design)
items.text: Finding Decision Stickiness made the result depend on history. Channels go by rank, then position, without history; only members of auto and people keep their slots. Incumbency as a tie-breaker (proposed) would break the example the same way, so ties go to the leftmost slot. "Holds" and "shows" are separate terms. Pools: circular, no order, auto_hold missing, no per-place options or ids. See the third review for the final rules; hold; options for a place and id. launch unreachable behind a condition; the Mic's Rec indicator hidden. Pitfalls section and check-config warnings. Paging, person strips, pick, collapse_hold had no home. Paging of people; type = "person"; pick as today; absent_after. Overrides vs delays, persistence, mode select without auto, when ORed with sources, loops, the chord freezing slots. Overrides bypass delays; one persistence rule (third review); auto in the mode select; when exclusive; loops are errors; chord buttons don't hold slots. Expression language. Grammar; one namespace with reserved words; pools without a prefix; tags named after kinds; errors with positions. GUI: Simulate, grid explosion, why not, cards, overridden style. All adopted. Home Assistant: feeding states, the mode select, formats, attributes. homeassistant = true with an input switch; formats and attributes defined. Daemon: batching, dwell, startup, reload, polling, logging, voice_chat. All adopted. Migration notes, deliberately empty slots. Adopted; "-".

items.title: Third review (the same profile, with hand traces of the example)
items.text: Finding Decision Blocker: pools and fall-through were circular; the steps didn't say how they iterate. Pools always hold (like channels); if present with pool presence counted before assignment; conditions depend only on inputs; the steps run once each, in order. Blocker: an exhausted stack and a held slot were undefined; motor moves of touchless faders. An implicit trailing auto ("-" for dark); held and dwelling slots are fixed inputs whose channel is reserved; motor moves don't count. Blocker: the example's table showed a scene that barely exists (people present means call with Mumble) and slot 8 changed twice. The example asked people if gaming and present and dropped Browser from slot 8 (replaced after the live test: people share auto). Blocker: a hidden channel's streams in auto had two owners. auto hands out whatever plays and has no slot, hidden apps channels as a whole; in_auto = false opts out. Blocker: four contradictions (meter_point, buds as state and channel, switching.hold, the noisy slot 4). meter_point on channels and places; the state is wireless; switching.hold goes; slot 4 removed from the example. Options for a place leaked entity ownership; options of today's auto strips missing. Look options on any candidate; control options and id on pool candidates only; the missing ones added. Pools of channels: shown twice, priority inverted, collapse migration too broad, Select. Members exclude channels with a slot; pools of channels fill by order; collapse migrates to if present in place; Select pages only on people. Three persistence rules; startup as an edge. One rule; overrides are kept across restarts; startup is the baseline. Entity ID collisions; shared homeassistant strips in migration. Reserved ids; one channel for shared entities. pick changed meaning. As today. Coverage: chord syntax, mode --next, the CLI, person name overlap, ignore vs exclude, auto_hold, the live device in the GUI, Mumble outside its slots. All adopted. Minor: banner and flashes, chip text, the presets link, cycle order, why for channels. All adopted. Newcomer configuration and init-config. A new configuration.

items.title: Design: previews of the controls
items.text: Status: built (2026-11-17).

items.title: Problem
items.text: The form of a channel lists its options, with help under each. What they do on the device has to be imagined: which LEDs a rec = "recording" lights and when, how the ring of a balance encoder looks, whether the meter of a pre_fader strip stays up while the fader goes down.

items.title: Idea
items.text:
The form of a channel (and of the pools [pool.apps], [pool.people] and [pool.auto]) groups its options by the part of the strip they are about, in the order of the device from top to bottom, each in a card:

Group Options Preview What it controls device, choices, profiles, match, person, launch, ... none Encoder encoder the encoder with its ring Display label, color, talking_color, lit_when_idle the LCD Buttons rec, solo, select Rec, Solo, Mute, Select Fader and meter fader, min_volume, max_volume, meter, meter_point the meter and the fader Slots absent_after, in_pool, tags none

The card of a part has a small drawing of that part on its left: the same drawing as the window Device (a StripView, cut to the part), so it looks exactly like the device. It shows a short scene, a step at a time like pictures (‹ and ›, with "2 / 4" between them), with a caption under it that says what happens, e.g. for rec = "recording":

  1. "Audio plays": Rec dark.
  2. "An application records": Rec lit.
  3. "Muted": Mute lit.

The scene follows the values in the form at once (also unsaved ones, and the defaults of unset options), and stays at the step shown, so changing an option shows its effect right there. (A first version played the steps in a loop: too fast to follow.)

items.title: Scenes
items.text:
• Encoder (encoder): volume turns the volume up in steps (ring filling, wrap), a push goes back to behavior.reset_volume; balance turns from the center to the right (boost_cut), a push centers it; pick steps through applications (dot), a push pins one (wrap); media seeks forward in a track, a push pauses; homeassistant turns a number.
  • Display: plays (label, volume), the fader moves (the new volume), muted, nothing to control (dark, or lit with lit_when_idle). People: there, talks (talking_color), away.
  • Buttons: plays, records, the default device (output and input only), muted, nothing plays. Each LED lights in the situations its indicator stands for; Mute in the muted one; Select while the device is the default (select).
  • Fader and meter: the fader at the bottom, at the 0 dB mark (with a range across 100 %) and at the top, with the volume of each place (min_volume, max_volume, behavior.unity_at) in the caption; the meter shows a steady level before the fader (pre_fader), or one that follows it (post_fader), and what a mute does to it.

items.title: Parts
items.text:
• gui/domain/demos.py (no Qt): the groups (GROUPS), and scene(part, strip_type, values, behavior), the frames (Frame: a caption and a StripState) from the resolved values. Tested without a window.
  • gui/qt/preview/part_view.py: PartView, a StripView cut to a part with ‹ and › to step through the frames.
  • StripView takes any StripHost (the Preview of the window Device, or a PartView).
  • ChannelsPage builds a card per group.

items.title: Not now
items.text: • Previews in the inspector of the page Slots (the options of a place). The same groups fit there.

items.title: A simulated device
items.text: Status: built (2026-11-17). Extended 2026-11-18: Select and Play above the drawing, Play also on the device of a running daemon (the live-view request play), and "Try without a device", which starts a daemon with the virtual device from the GUI (see the decisions below).

items.title: Why
items.text:
The X-Touch Extender used for development was defective (the touch sensors of faders 1 and 4 failed) and went back. Without a device nothing above the protocol can be tried outside the tests: no slots on strips, no fader under a finger while a slot changes, no LEDs and texts to look at. The protocol and the behavior of the device are known well (see Hardware, verified on the device on 2026-11-15), so a simulated device can stand in for it: for development, for the GUI, and for tests that run the real Surface end to end.

The model is also how the GUI sees the device (decided 2026-11-17): the daemon keeps one as a mirror of the device it drives, and the GUI shows the mirror. One model of the device, then, for the virtual device, the GUI and the tests.

items.title: Goals
items.text:
• The daemon talks to the simulated device with the same bytes as to the real one. Everything above the transport (Surface, its touch grace, touchless faders, the glide of the motors, the startup sequence, reconnects) runs unchanged, so it gets tried too.
  • The simulated device behaves like the real one where Hardware says how, including faults: a touch sensor that fails (like the returned unit), the device switched off and on (faders move by themselves), unplugged.
  • One model of the device, without IO and without Qt, behind its frontends: the mirror in the daemon (what the GUI shows), a socket server for the daemon, the GUI's drawing to use it, and a test fixture.
  • No root, no kernel modules: it has to work in CI and in a user session.

Not a goal: proving timing-sensitive motor behavior (slow moves, the stop short of the bottom, motor noise). The simulator models the motor simply; those need the real device.

items.title: Rejected: a virtual ALSA MIDI device
items.text: The kernel's snd-virmidi makes raw MIDI devices that Surface would find in /proc/asound/cards without any change. But it needs modprobe (root), its other end is the ALSA sequencer (a second API for the simulator), and it doesn't work in CI. A transport of our own is simpler and testable.

items.title: 1. A transport seam in Surface
items.text:
Today Surface.open() finds the card in /proc/asound/cards and opens /dev/snd/midiC<card>D0 as RawMidi.

  • hardware/transport.py: a Transport protocol with what Surface uses of RawMidi (write, drain, close, is_open; data and the end come through the callbacks on_data and on_closed). RawMidi is one.
  • A Port finds and opens a transport, LookupError when there is no device (as today):
  • AlsaPort(device_name, proc_asound_cards, dev_snd): today's code, moved out of Surface.open().
  • SocketPort(path): connects to the simulator's Unix socket. No simulator running is "not connected", so Surface.run() waits and connects when it starts, and a closed simulator is an unplugged device: the reconnect path gets used.
  • Surface(port=...); the daemon picks the port from the configuration: [device] virtual = true (or xtouch-daemon run --virtual-device, which wins) uses SocketPort(instance.virtual_device_socket_file()), next to the other runtime files ($XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/xtouch-daemon/).
  • The log says which: "Connected to the simulated X-Touch-Ext at ...".

items.title: 2. The messages to the device, decoded
items.text:
hardware/protocol.py builds the messages to the device (fader, led, ring, meter, lcd_text, lcd_colors) and decodes those from it. The simulator needs the other direction:

  • decode_host(message) -> HostEvent | None with MotorMoved(strip, value), LedSet(strip, button, Led), RingSet(strip, position, mode, center), MeterSet(strip, level), LcdText(offset, text), LcdColors(colors).
  • And the encoders for what the device sends: fader_moved, fader_touched, button, encoder_turned, encoder_pressed, host_query.
  • Round-trip tests: every encoder against its decoder, both directions, over the full value ranges.

items.title: 3. The model: simulator/device.py
items.text:
SimulatedDevice, pure (no IO, no asyncio, no Qt): it takes bytes from the host and the time, and gives bytes for the host. Time comes in as an argument (now), so tests and frontends drive it.

State per strip:

  • LCD: two lines of 7 characters (written by offset into the 2 x 56 characters, as the device does), and the color.
  • The LEDs of Rec, Solo, Mute and Select: off, on, flashing.
  • The ring: position 0..11, mode, center LED.
  • The meter: the level and when it was set; it falls by itself. The rate of the fall is not measured: about one level per 150 ms, marked as an assumption (see "Fidelity").
  • The fader: where it is (14 bits, but positions in multiples of 4 as the device reports them), the motor's target, touched or not. The motor goes to the target at a fixed speed (about 100 ms over the whole range), not while touched; a motor move sends nothing back (the real device doesn't either).
  • The encoder: pressed or not.

Input (what a hand does), each returning the bytes the device sends:

  • touch(strip, touched), move(strip, fraction): a move while not touched follows the real device: with touch_delay (default 0.07 s) the touch comes after the first moves, as with a quick hand.
  • press(strip, button, pressed), turn(strip, steps), push(strip, pressed).

Faults and events:

  • broken_touch: set[int]: these faders never report a touch (the returned unit: {0, 3}).
  • power_cycle(): sends the host query, then the faders go down by themselves (moves without a touch), as after switching the device on; texts, colors and LEDs are gone until the host sends them again.
  • The host query on connect: F0 00 00 66 15 01 <serial> <challenge> F7 with a made-up serial.
  • Unplugging is the frontends' business (they close the connection).

A changed callback (or a version counter) tells frontends to repaint.

items.title: 4. The mirror: what the GUI shows
items.text:
The Surface keeps a SimulatedDevice as the mirror of the device: every byte it sends goes into it (also while the device is away: then it is what the device will show once it is there), and what the device sends goes in too (observe(): fader moves, touches, encoder pushes). The device's query after switching on changes nothing: the Surface shows everything again on each connect, and after one the mirror doesn't know where the faders are until the motor moved them or the device reported a move (forget_faders()). The live view's strips are the mirror's state (strip_states()), so the GUI shows what reached the device, banners and flashes included, with the motor and the meters moving as the model moves them. The Surface keeps its own record of what each strip shows only where it needs it to send (the strips' values and looks).

What the mirror can't know: what the device does without saying (a motor that stopped short, where the faders are after a connect). It shows what was sent and what the device reported.

items.title: 5. The virtual device and its frontends
items.text:
simulator/server.py: a Unix socket server at instance.virtual_device_socket_file() with one SimulatedDevice. One client at a time (the daemon); a second one is refused, like a device another program has open. A tick (every 10 ms) moves the motors and lets the meters fall. The same device stays when the daemon disconnects and connects again, so a daemon restart sees the faders where they were, as on the real device.

  • CLI: xtouch-daemon virtual-device runs the server headless, logs what the host sets at debug level, and takes a few options (--broken-touch 1,4). (Not simulate: that one simulates slots.)
  • GUI: the GUI can host the server itself (a QLocalServer around the same SimulatedDevice). Then its drawing of the device takes the mouse, sent to the hosted device as a hand:
  • a fader: press = touch, drag = moves, release = let go; Alt-drag moves it without a touch;
  • the buttons: click (press and release), held while the mouse is down;
  • the encoder: the wheel turns it, a click pushes it;
  • a toolbar: plug in / unplug, switch off and on, broken touch per fader.

What it paints still comes from the live view (the daemon's mirror), which is the hosted device's state once it got there; the GUI doesn't paint two models. While the daemon waits for a device that isn't connected, the pill "X-Touch-Ext not connected" offers "Open the virtual device"; nothing starts without a click. - Tests: a fixture that connects a real Surface to a SimulatedDevice through an in-memory transport (no socket), with the loop's clock (looptime). New end-to-end tests: touch grace, touchless faders, the glide arriving, the startup sequence, a power cycle, a reconnect, a slot change under a finger. RecordingSurface stays for the tests that only look at what was sent.

items.title: 6. Fidelity
items.text: What the simulator does is either verified on the device (it says so in Hardware) or an assumption; the assumptions are listed in the module's docstring and in the docs: the speed of the motor, the fall of the meters, the delay of the touch, the moves after switching on. A test against the real device later replaces assumptions with measurements.

items.title: The order of the work
items.text:
Each step is a commit with its tests, docs and CHANGELOG entry; the daemon works after each.

  1. Protocol (done): the decoders of the messages to the device and the encoders of those from it.
  2. Model (done): SimulatedDevice with its state, the input, the motor and meter over time, and the faults.
  3. Transport (done): Port, AlsaPort, SocketPort; Surface(port=...); [device] virtual, run --virtual-device; the in-memory transport and the test fixture; end-to-end tests of the Surface.
  4. Mirror (done): the Surface feeds its SimulatedDevice, strip_states() reads it; the GUI's drawing shows it.
  5. Server and CLI (done): simulator/server.py, xtouch-daemon virtual-device; a test of the daemon against the server over a real socket (connect, unplug, reconnect, a second client refused).
  6. GUI (done): hosting the virtual device, the mouse on the drawing, the toolbar, the offer in the pill; GUI tests.
  7. Docs (done): "Without a device" in Getting started, the simulator in Hardware (what is verified, what is assumed), GUI, Commands, Configuration ([device] virtual), the architecture page.

items.title: Decisions (2026-11-17)
items.text:
• The CLI command is xtouch-daemon virtual-device, the option [device] virtual = true, and xtouch-daemon run --virtual-device overrides it.
  • The GUI offers the virtual device but doesn't start it: while the daemon waits for a device that isn't connected, the pill "X-Touch-Ext not connected" has "Open the virtual device". Nothing starts without a click.
  • (2026-11-18) The mouse on the drawing is a hand only in Play; Select (the default) picks and moves slots. Play also works on the device of a running daemon through the live view (live.Play, Surface.play()), so the GUI is a remote control for the real device too. While no daemon runs, "Try without a device" starts one with the virtual device on the file and hosts it: a demo for people without the device. It is the one thing the GUI starts by itself, and only on that click; it ends with the window.

items.title: Design: output choices and strips that move
items.text:
Status: implemented on feature/dynamic-strips; see Decisions and deviations at the end.

Two features:

  1. Choices (A): one strip switches between several outputs (or inputs), each optionally in its own sound card profile. For example Phones (analog), Speaker (digital) and Buds (Bluetooth), cycled with Select.
  2. Collapsing strips (B): a strip that has nothing to control gives up its fader, and the strips after it move left to fill the gap. A configuration can list more than 8 strips; the first 8 that are present get the faders.

They are independent, but they compose: a strip with choices is absent when none of its choices is there.

items.title: Motivation
items.text:
The author's setup has three outputs: analog headphones and a digital speaker on one sound card (two profiles), and Bluetooth headphones that come and go. Only one is used at a time. Today this takes two or three strips, or one strip where Select switches the device and Rec switches the card profile. That second way is two buttons, and Rec does nothing while the Bluetooth device is shown.

When the Bluetooth headphones are off, their strip is dead: a fader for nothing. The strips after it (Browser, ...) should move up and use it.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
A new option choices on output and input strips: a list of tables.

[[strip]]
type = "output"
color = "cyan"

[[strip.choices]]
label = "Phones"
device = "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.analog-stereo"
card = "alsa_card.pci-0000_11_00.4"
profile = "output:analog-stereo+input:analog-stereo"

[[strip.choices]]
label = "Speaker"
device = "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.iec958-stereo"
card = "alsa_card.pci-0000_11_00.4"
profile = "output:iec958-stereo+input:analog-stereo"
max_volume = 200

[[strip.choices]]
label = "Buds"
device = "bluez_output.*"

(The first draft wrote the choices as inline tables over several lines; TOML 1.0, which tomllib reads, does not allow line breaks in an inline table. See below.)

The keys of a choice:

Key Required Meaning device yes The node name or description, */? wildcards allowed (like device today). With a wildcard, the first matching device. label no The top line of the LCD while this choice is active. By default, the start of the device's description, as today. card with profile The sound card (name or description, wildcards allowed) whose profile has to be set for this choice. profile no The card profile (name or description) the choice needs. Without it, the choice uses the device as it is. min_volume, max_volume no The volume range while this choice is active, like on profiles today.

Validation (pydantic, with clear messages, as check-config shows them): - choices needs at least 2 entries. - choices excludes device and profiles on the same strip ("use either choices or device/profiles"). - profile needs card, and card needs profile. - select = false with choices is an error: Select is how one switches. - Labels are optional; duplicates are allowed but get a warning-level problem in the GUI, if the GUI has warnings (check).

Keep device and profiles working unchanged. choices is the new way for the switching case, and docs point to it. No migration of existing files.

items.title: Behavior
items.text:
• Available: a choice is available when its device exists. A choice with card/profile is also available when the card exists and has that profile (its device appears only after the switch).
  • Active: the strip shows the active choice: the one whose device is the default (for output, the default output; for input, the default input). If none is the default, it shows the one shown last, if it is still available, else the first available one.
  • Select press: goes to the next available choice after the active one, wrapping around. It:
  • switches the card to the choice's profile first, if the choice has one and the card is not in it. Reuse the _Switch mechanism of strips/device.py: the label shows at once, the device is awaited, and on failure the strip goes back.
  • then makes the choice's device the default. A press while a switch is still pending goes on from the pending target, so fast presses step through the choices.
  • Select LED: on while the active choice's device is the default (same meaning as today).
  • Rec: keeps its normal rec indicator meaning (recording etc.). It is no longer used for profiles on this strip.
  • Label: the choice's label, else the description start (as today).
  • Volume range: the choice's min_volume/max_volume, else the strip's, else [behavior].
  • Fader/mute/encoder: act on the active choice's device, as they do on a device strip today.
  • Nothing available: the strip behaves like a device strip whose device is missing (as today). With B, it is absent (see below).
  • Moved elsewhere: if the default changes elsewhere (pavucontrol, a Bluetooth connect where WirePlumber makes the headphones the default), the strip follows it when the new default is one of its choices.
  • Two choices on the same card in the same profile: both are available, and switching between them only changes the default.

items.title: Home Assistant
items.text: The existing entities of output strips keep working. Add a select entity for a strip with choices (select.<ns>_<id>_output), with the labels as options: choosing one in Home Assistant switches like Select does. Follow how the layouts branch registers its select.<ns>_layout entity.

items.title: CLI
items.text:
• xtouch-daemon list-devices must show cards and their profiles (name and description), so card and profile can be filled in. Check what it shows today, and add what's missing.
  • check-config describes a choices strip ("output: Phones, Speaker or Buds (Select switches)").

items.title: GUI
items.text:
• A table editor for choices on output/input strips. Columns: label, device, card, profile, min/max volume. Use the existing Tables field of fields.py.
  • Pickers come from the sound server state the GUI already reads: devices for device, cards for card, the profiles of the chosen card for profile.
  • device/profiles and choices exclude each other. The GUI shows the one in use; switching between them keeps the other's values, like the kept-options feature does for strip types.
  • Explanations and doc links, like the other options (gui/domain/docs.py, the meanings in config.py).
  • The device preview shows the active choice's label. Offline (no live view), it shows the first choice.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
A new option on every strip type except empty and homeassistant:

[[strip]]
type = "output"
device = "bluez_output.*"
label = "Buds"
collapse = true          # gives its fader to the strips after it while no Bluetooth headphones are there

And in [behavior]:

[behavior]
collapse_hold = 3        # seconds a strip stays after it became absent, before the strips after it move
  • collapse (bool, default false).
  • collapse_hold (seconds, default 3, ≥ 0).
  • More than 8 strips: allowed, up to a sane maximum (32). Validation fails if there are more than 8 strips and fewer than count - 8 of them have collapse = true, since some strips could then never get a fader. The message says which strips can never show.
  • homeassistant strips can't collapse: their entities are always there, and automations rely on them.
  • empty can't collapse either: it exists to reserve a place.

items.title: When a strip is absent
items.text:
Type Absent while output, input none of its devices (device patterns, or the available choices) exists. With device unset (the default device), never. apps none of its applications has a stream (playing or paused). auto it has no application assigned (after auto_hold). voip (layouts) the provider reports no participant for it. inherit (layouts) its resolved strip is absent.

A strip becomes absent only after it has been absent for collapse_hold seconds. It becomes present again at once. Both changes are debounced per update: one placement per audio state update.

items.title: Placement
items.text:
The strips are a flow, in config order (after layout resolution, see below). The physical strips 1..8 show the first 8 strips that are present or don't collapse. Remaining physical strips (fewer than 8 present) show nothing: dark, faders down, like an empty strip. Strips beyond those 8 wait off the device.

Example (the author's case):

config:  Out(choices)  Buds(collapse)  Browser  Games  VoIP  auto  auto  Mic  Spotify(collapse, apps)
no Buds: Out           Browser         Games    VoIP   auto  auto  Mic   Spotify
Buds on: Out           Buds            Browser  Games  VoIP  auto  auto  Mic       (Spotify waits)

Rules: - Identity: a strip's state (controller, held auto app, pending switches, volumes, meters) belongs to its config entry, not to the physical strip. Moving a strip moves its controller to another physical strip: LCD, LEDs, ring and fader (the motor glides to the controller's value) follow. - Don't move under a finger: while any fader is touched, or any button is held, placement changes wait (up to the release). Check how the layouts branch defers a layout switch, and reuse that. - Home Assistant ids: the default strip_<position> id of a strip is its config position (1-based in the layout's list), not the physical one. Today the two are the same, so nothing changes for existing setups. Document this. - The meter capture follows the controller (the capture targets are a function of the controllers on the device). - Logging: each placement change at info level: "Strips: Buds appears at 2, Browser moves to 3, Spotify waits".

items.title: Interaction with layouts
items.text: Each layout is a strip list, a flow. inherit resolves first. Then the flow places the resolved list. A layout switch places from scratch (no hold). Per-layout placement is independent: collapsed state is computed from the current audio state, so no state is carried between layouts beyond the per-entry hold timers of the default layout's strips. If that is complex, a switch may simply reset the hold timers.

items.title: Live protocol and GUI
items.text:
• Snapshot: add the assignment, e.g. placement: tuple[int | None, ...]. For each physical strip, the index of the config strip it shows, or None. It is optional and versioned, like the other later fields, so an older GUI and an older daemon keep working.
  • Device preview in the GUI: shows the live placement while the daemon tells it. Clicking a physical strip selects the config strip it shows. Offline: the static placement with every strip present.
  • Editor: every config strip has to be reachable, including those beyond 8 and the collapsed ones. Add a compact strip list or overflow row (the implementer picks; follow docs/development/architecture.md's GUI section once the GUI architecture rework has landed). It shows which strips are on the device now, which are collapsed, and which wait.
  • Option order: collapse goes with the strip-level options (the GUI agent is making the order follow the device; put it near the top, after the type-specific "what it controls" fields).
  • "Add strip" works beyond 8 only when that stays valid (see validation), otherwise it explains why not.

items.title: Docs
items.text:
• A page docs/configuration/collapsing.md (or a section in strips.md), with the example above.
  • A clear note: moving strips are bad for muscle memory. The fader under your finger may control something else than a minute ago. The feature is opt-in for that reason. The LCD labels say what each strip is.
  • Devices docs: choices, with the Phones/Speaker/Buds example, and how to find card and profile (list-devices).
  • check-config output, the GUI page, CHANGELOG, config.example.toml (commented examples).

items.title: C. inherit from any layout and strip
items.text:
Added later, at the user's request. Today an inherit strip takes the strip of the default layout at its place. It can name another layout and another strip:

[[layout.strip]]
type = "inherit"
layout = "voice"   # optional, by default the default layout (as today)
strip = 3          # optional: a 1-based position in that layout's list, or a strip `id` string; by default the same place
  • Validation: an unknown layout or strip is an error, and so is a strip id that more than one strip of that layout has. Chains (an inherit of an inherit) resolve, up to a limit; a loop is an error that names the cycle.
  • voip with count > 1: decide and document. (Later moot: count is gone, see the decisions.)
  • Resolution before the flow (B): a referenced strip that collapses collapses here too. It carries all its options along, also launch.
  • State: the state of a strip that several layouts share (the held application of an auto strip, a pending switch) is shared: the same entry is the same controller, so a layout switch does not lose it. If that is hard given how layouts build controllers, decide and document.
  • Home Assistant: a referenced homeassistant strip keeps the entity ids of its source (its id or its position there), and its entities are not registered twice.
  • check-config, the GUI (pickers for layout and strip on inherit strips; the preview shows the referenced strip), docs (layouts.md), CHANGELOG, tests.

items.title: Implementation notes
items.text:
• Config: config.py. Choices are a ChoiceConfig model. collapse goes on _StripConfig (with validators that refuse it on homeassistant/empty). Raise the strip count limit with the collapse validation. Keep config.py's field order for the TOML/comment output sensible; the GUI's order is its own (explicit order in the GUI schema).
  • Strips: strips/device.py gets the choices logic (maybe a ChoicesController next to DeviceController, sharing the profile-switch code). Each controller type gets absent(state) -> bool.
  • Placement: a pure function place(strips, present, held) -> tuple[int | None, ...], fully unit-tested. A small owner (in the mixer, or wherever layouts switch strips) applies changes: rebinds controllers to surface strips and defers during touches. Hardware interactions timed or racing must be in a strictly typed state, not loose dicts.
  • Tests: fake backend scenarios.
  • A Bluetooth device appears: Buds shows at 2, Browser moves to 3, the faders glide.
  • It disappears: after collapse_hold the strips move back, not before.
  • A touched fader defers the move, which happens on release.
  • Choices cycle through all three, the profile switch then the default, and a failed switch reverts.
  • A pending switch plus a second press goes to the next one.
  • HA select switches the choice.
  • Snapshot placement round trip; the GUI preview shows the placement.
  • Validation messages.
  • Coverage stays at 100 % (AGENTS.md).
  • Docs build strict. just lint, pyright 0 errors.

items.title: Later
items.text:
• pin = true: a strip that keeps its physical position while others flow around it.
  • A layout rule on device presence (devices = ["bluez_output.*"]), as an alternative to collapsing.

items.title: Decisions and deviations
items.text:
What the implementation decided where this document was open, wrong, or contradicted the code.

  • TOML: inline tables can't span lines in TOML 1.0 (tomllib), so the example of the first draft did not parse. The docs use [[strip.choices]] tables; a one-line inline table per choice works as well.
  • Select on a choice that is shown but not the default makes it the default first instead of skipping to the next one, like Select on a device strip. Otherwise the LED would be off and the first press would leave the choice shown.
  • A finished default switch ends the pending switch when the command returns, not only when the state shows the new default: a default that the sound server never reports (another program changes it right back) must not pin the strip to the choice.
  • card takes a description too: the Card model got its description (device.description of the card), which list-devices now shows next to the name. The profiles were already listed with name and description.
  • Home Assistant select: its options are the titles of the choices (label, else device); a second choice of the same title gets a number (Out 2), since the options of a select must differ. The entity is created with [mqtt] only and its id is <id>_output or <id>_input after the strip type. It joins the duplicate-id check (Config.entity_strips()), not home_assistant_strips(), so a strip with choices does not need [mqtt].
  • Duplicate labels are allowed and get no warning: the GUI has no warning level yet (only errors).
  • Validation of strips that can never show: the rule "fewer than count - 8 strips with collapse" lets e.g. 8 steady strips followed by a collapsing one through, which could never show. The check is per strip: a strip with 8 steady strips before it never gets a fader. The message names those strips. The limit is 32 places (voip counted count until it was removed). An inherit strip beyond the strips of the default layout is an error too.
  • Collapsed stays collapsed: a strip that collapsed stays so until it is present again, also when it collapsed without a hold (from scratch). Each strip has one typed record (placement._Absence).
  • Deferring under a finger: layouts don't defer their switches (they switch at once), so there was nothing to reuse. The mixer follows the touches, held buttons and encoder pushes from the device's events and the surface's held faders, and Flow waits while any is there; the release places what waited. The meter tick (every 0.1 s) places a hold time that ended without a new state.
  • Without a sound server nothing moves (the absences are unknown); the first state places from scratch.
  • Layout switches and reloads reset the hold timers: a new mixer places from scratch, as the document allowed.
  • Snapshot versioning: the live view never bumps VERSION for new fields; later fields are optional with a default (mqtt_state, layout, ...). placement is the same: None from an older daemon. It holds indexes of Config.all_strips(layout): the TOML list, with inherit resolved and auto strips up to 8. (While a voip strip had count places, these were places, and Config.places() mapped them to the list; both went with count.)
  • absent of apps strips looks at streams only: a paused media player (MPRIS) without a stream does not keep a collapsing strip.
  • auto strips beyond the device take applications too (the assigner fills slots in config order), so an application may go to a waiting auto strip when all on the device are taken.
  • voip strips collapse one by one, so with collapse an empty call takes no faders and the strips of the group that a small one leaves over give theirs up. (First each place of a voip strip with count; since count is gone, each voip strip, see Design: layouts.)
  • C, voip strips: decided first: strip = N named an entry of the list, so a voip strip with count came with all its places, and an inherit without strip took one of them. Superseded: every voip strip is one strip now, so there is nothing special. An inherited voip strip is one of the voip strips of the layout it lands in: with person a fixed strip there, without it a strip of that layout's group.
  • C, the same place: "the same place" is the position in the list, also for another layout. Positions after the strips of that layout are auto strips up to 8; beyond that it is an error.
  • C, state is not shared across layouts: a layout switch builds a new mixer with new controllers (as reloads do); keeping some controllers alive across mixers would mean moving them between VirtualStrips, flows and the auto assigner, and inherited strips never kept their state before either. So an auto strip takes the application that plays at the switch (usually the same one), and a pending choice switch is cancelled with the old strip (StripController.close()), maybe after the profile switched; the new strip shows the default device as it is then. Documented in layouts.md.
  • C, Home Assistant ids: a strip without id that lands on another place than its own gets the id of its own place (strip_<n>), so a referenced homeassistant strip, fader or choices select keeps its entities. The ids of all layouts are one set, so they are registered once. The same strip twice in one layout is the existing duplicate-id error.
  • C, top-level inherit: allowed when it names a layout or strip (a bare one would refer to itself).
  • C, errors are of the whole file: like the other layout checks they are model errors, so the GUI lists them in the problems, not next to the strip; the preview shows such a strip as "?".
  • C, GUI preview by position: the GUI resolves inherit by list position, like the daemon. (While voip strips had count, the daemon went by places, and the two differed after such a strip.)

items.title: Design: launching applications from a strip
items.text:
Status: implemented as described here; how to use it is in Applications and VoIP.

The idea: the Select button of a strip whose application is not there starts it. A "VoIP" strip starts Mumble and connects it to the server, a "Music" strip starts the music player.

items.title: Where Select is free
items.text:
Strip type What Select does without launch launch output, input makes the device the default (select), or nothing not allowed: Select is taken apps nothing allowed auto nothing allowed voip shows the next page of participants (the LED is on while there are several pages) allowed: Select launches while the voice chat is not there, and pages as before while it is homeassistant an event in Home Assistant not allowed: Home Assistant owns the strip and can never send a command empty, inherit nothing / the inherited strip's not allowed / the inherited strip's

Validation is by pydantic: an unknown option on the other types is an error already (extra = "forbid").

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
[[strip]]
type = "apps"
match = ["discord", "webrtc", "teamspeak", "ts3client", "signal", "mumble"]
label = "VoIP"
launch = ["mumble", "mumble://markus@voice.example.org/Gaming"]
  • launch: the program, then its arguments, as a list. It must not be empty, and no part may be empty.
  • A single string is accepted too and split with shlex.split (quotes like a shell, nothing expanded: no ~, $VAR, globs, pipes or &&). Decided for it because a command line is what people copy from a .desktop file or a terminal, and the GUI's list of chips stays the canonical form (it saves a list). The split happens at validation, so check-config and the GUI show the parts.
  • launch_when_running (apps, auto): Select starts the command also while the application runs. For Mumble that is useful: a running Mumble takes the URL and connects (see below), and mumble without a URL brings its window to the front. Not on voip strips, where Select pages while the voice chat is there.

items.title: Mumble URLs
items.text:
From the Mumble documentation:

mumble://[username[:password]@]<address>[:port]/[channelpath][?title=<servername>][&url=<serverurl>]
  • The port defaults to 64738. Special characters of the channel path must be URL-encoded (Gaming%20Night). Subchannels are separated by /. When the channel can't be reached, Mumble stays in the default channel.
  • ?version=1.2.0 was needed only before Mumble 1.2.4. title and url matter only when the link is dropped into the server browser.
  • A password in the URL ends up in the configuration file and in the process list (/proc/*/cmdline is readable by every user). Leave it out and let Mumble remember it, or use a certificate.

A running Mumble accepts the URL too: on Linux, Mumble's main.cpp hands the URL of a second instance over D-Bus (openUrl on info.mumble.mumble, then the legacy net.sourceforge.mumble.mumble) to the running one and exits; without a URL it asks the running one to focus. Only --multiple starts a second client. Verified in the source (src/mumble/main.cpp), not with a real Mumble.

items.title: When an application "runs"
items.text:
Select launches only while none of the strip's applications runs. "Runs" for each type:

Strip type Runs while apps a stream matches match, or a process whose name contains one of the match entries runs, or the program of launch runs auto the strip has an application (it plays, was picked, or its hold time is not over), or the program of launch runs voip the provider reports the voice chat (connected: the Mumble plugin is there, also while nobody talks), or the program of launch runs
  • Processes are matched like the processes rule of layouts (layouts.process_matching()): the names from layouts.running_processes() (the kernel's comm and the file name of the program, in lower case), containing the pattern. So a silent Mumble (no stream) counts as running.
  • The program of launch is the file name of its first part, matched exactly, not as a part: flatpak must not match flatpak-portal, which runs all the time. For ["flatpak", "run", "info.mumble.Mumble"] that is useless (the program is flatpak), so name the application in match (mumble matches the process inside the sandbox).
  • The processes are read every 2 s (mixer.PROCESS_INTERVAL, like the layout rules), only while a strip of the layout has launch.
  • A match entry like signal also counts unrelated processes whose name contains it. The cost is a Select that does nothing; list-apps and ps -e show what runs.

items.title: Starting it
items.text:
• Never through a shell. The list goes to exec as it is.
  • Detached from the daemon's service. With a systemd user manager (its socket $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/systemd/private) and systemd-run in PATH: systemd-run --user --quiet --collect --unit=xtouch-launch-<program>-<random> --property=WorkingDirectory=~ -- argv…. Otherwise a plain process in a session of its own (start_new_session), stdin/stdout/stderr on /dev/null, waited for by a thread so it does not stay a zombie.
  • Deviation from the first idea, systemd-run --scope: a scope runs the command as a child of systemd-run, which is a child of the daemon, with the daemon's environment. The daemon's service starts with default.target, often before the desktop imports WAYLAND_DISPLAY/DISPLAY into the user manager, so a GUI application started from a scope may find no display. A transient service gets the user manager's environment of the moment, is not a child of the daemon (no zombie, survives a restart of the daemon without question), and its output goes to the journal (journalctl --user -u 'xtouch-launch-*'). --collect removes the unit also when it failed.
  • Logging: every start is logged (info, with the command), a program that is not in PATH is a warning (checked before, with shutil.which, so systemd-run does not fail later in the background), an OSError of the start a warning, an exit of the started process with an error code (fallback mode, or systemd-run itself) a warning. A launch that does not show up in 15 s is a warning. Nothing of it stops the daemon.
  • Debounce: no second launch within 5 s (LAUNCH_DEBOUNCE) of the last one while the application is not up yet, so a double press starts it once.
  • Reload: the launch state belongs to the strip and starts anew with a reload or a layout switch; the started application is not affected.

items.title: The Select LED
items.text:
Strip type LED with launch apps, auto flashes while launching (until the application runs, at most 15 s, LAUNCH_TIMEOUT), on while it runs, off otherwise. Without launch it stays off, as before. voip flashes while launching, then as before: on while there are several pages. "On while it runs" would hide the paging, which is the older meaning.

The device flashes the LED itself (Mackie Control Led.FLASH), the daemon sends it once.

items.title: Security
items.text:
• Commands come only from the configuration: the file, or the configuration of a live preview. The live view only accepts clients of the same user (SO_PEERCRED in live.py), who could edit the file anyway. A preview whose launch runs something is no more than that user can do in a shell.
  • Home Assistant and MQTT can never send a command: nothing arriving over MQTT reaches launch, and homeassistant strips can't have it.
  • No Home Assistant button entity for now. A button per strip that runs the configured command would be safe (it runs only the configured command, never one from MQTT), but it lets anyone who can press buttons in Home Assistant start programs on the desktop, also while nobody sits there. Left out until there is a use for it.

items.title: Later
items.text:
• Focus the window when Select is pressed while the application runs. On Wayland there is no portable way (KWin scripts, GNOME extensions, the Sway/Hyprland IPC differ, see Layouts). For Mumble, launch_when_running with launch = ["mumble"] already does it through Mumble's own D-Bus focus.
  • A launch_process option for commands whose program is not the application (flatpak run, gtk-launch), if match turns out not to be enough.
  • A Home Assistant button (see Security).

items.title: Design: layouts
items.text:
Status: implemented as in Phasing; how to use it is in Channels, states and slots, which replaced layouts.

The idea: the configuration holds several layouts, each a set of up to 8 strips. A "default" layout for the desk (outputs, browser, music), a "gaming" layout with the game, the voice chat, the microphone and one strip per participant of the voice channel. Something switches between them: Home Assistant, an application that starts or plays, a button combination on the device, the command line or the GUI.

items.title: What others do
items.text:
Product Unit How it switches Notes Elgato Stream Deck profile, with pages and folders "Smart Profiles": the application in focus picks its profile, matched by executable; leaving it restores the previous profile. A key action switches by hand. (Elgato) Automatic switching is paused while the editor is open. A manual switch by a plugin can disable the automatic one (bug report), a known pain point. Loupedeck / Logitech profile per application, with workspaces and pages "Dynamic mode" (on by default) follows the active application; off, the chosen profile stays. A button switches workspaces. (Loupedeck CT, user guide) Open-source Linux ports match by process name and window title, falling back to a default profile (loupedeckapp). GoXLR Utility (Linux) device and microphone profiles UI, and goxlr-client profiles device load <name> for scripts and hotkeys (wiki) The profile is a whole mixer state; a "load colours only" variant exists. Mackie Control DAWs (Logic, Cubase) banks of 8 channels Bank Left/Right moves by 8 (by the size of the surface group), Channel Left/Right by 1; the last bank is filled up to 8 rather than left half empty (Logic) The model for "more participants than strips". deej one configuration none; the file is reloaded on change (From the project's README, not re-checked.) Voicemeeter settings files, macro buttons macro buttons and the Remote API load a settings file (From memory, not re-checked.) TouchOSC pages (tabs) of one layout a tab bar on the surface, or OSC/MIDI messages (From memory, not re-checked.)

Lessons taken:

  1. One active layout, switched as a whole. Every product swaps the complete set of controls; nobody blends two.
  2. Automatic and manual switching coexist, and the rules for that must be simple. Stream Deck and Loupedeck make the automatic one win whenever the focus changes; a manual choice lasts until the next change. That is the model here too: rules are edge-triggered (see Switching).
  3. Focus is a desktop concept. On Wayland there is no portable way to ask which window has the focus (KWin scripts, GNOME extensions, the Sway/Hyprland IPC all differ). The daemon knows something better for a mixer: which applications play (PipeWire streams), and which processes run (/proc). Focus can come later as a provider of the same rule engine.
  4. A command line to switch (GoXLR) makes every other integration (hotkeys, scripts, desktop launchers) free.
  5. Banks for variable lists (Mackie): a group of strips shows a page of a longer list, and buttons page through it.

items.title: VoIP participants
items.text: The wish: a strip per participant of the voice channel, with the participant's level on the meter and their volume on the fader.

items.title: Can a mixer see the participants?
items.text:
Not through PipeWire. Mumble, TeamSpeak and Discord mix every participant into one playback stream, so pw-dump shows one node per client, never one per participant. The participants are only known inside the client.

Client Participants and talking Local volume per participant From outside on Linux Mumble (1.5) Plugin API: getUsersInChannel, getUserName, mumble_onUserTalkingStateChanged, onUserAdded/Removed Not in the API (requestLocalMute/isUserLocallyMuted mute only). But mumble_onAudioSourceFetched(pcm, …, isSpeech, userID) gets each participant's audio before the mix, may change it (a plugin can apply its own gain) and can measure its peak. The built-in local volume (since 1.3) is not reachable. (MumblePlugin.h) D-Bus net.sourceforge.mumble.mumble: getTalkingUsers, getCurrentUrl, self mute/deaf, transmit mode (DBus.h); mumble rpc the same few commands (RPC docs). No participant list, no per-user volume. Server side (Ice): users and channels, but no talking state and no client-local volume. TeamSpeak 3 ClientQuery (local TCP 25639, API key): clientlist, notifytalkstatuschange, notifycliententerview (client query library) Plugin SDK only: setClientVolumeModifier(connection, client, dB), and the client stores it (forum). No ClientQuery command for it was found. ClientQuery is reachable from another process. TeamSpeak ⅚ has no stable public API (not re-checked). Discord Local RPC (Unix socket discord-ipc-N): GET_SELECTED_VOICE_CHANNEL, SPEAKING_START/STOP events SET_USER_VOICE_SETTINGS (volume 0..200, mute) (Userdoccers) The rpc* scopes are for "approved partners" only (Discord OAuth2); projects use Discord's own StreamKit client id and token endpoint instead, without refresh tokens, and Discord restores the volumes when the app disconnects (Noctalia Discord Voice). Fragile and a ToS gray area.

So per-participant levels need code inside the client (a Mumble plugin, a TeamSpeak plugin). Per-participant volume needs the same (Mumble: the plugin applies its own gain in onAudioSourceFetched; TeamSpeak: setClientVolumeModifier), or Discord's restricted RPC. Participant lists and talking states alone are possible from outside for TeamSpeak (ClientQuery) and Discord (RPC), not for Mumble.

items.title: Recommendation: a pluggable provider, and a bridge
items.text:
graph LR
    Mumble[Mumble + plugin] -- "JSON lines" --> Bridge
    TS[TeamSpeak + plugin] -- "JSON lines" --> Bridge
    Bridge[BridgeProvider<br/>$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/xtouch-daemon-voip.sock] --> Strips[voip strips]
    Demo[DemoProvider] --> Strips
    Later[later: TeamSpeak ClientQuery, Discord RPC] -.-> Strips
  • VoipProvider (src/xtouch_daemon/voip/provider.py): a snapshot of Participants (id, name, talking, muted, volume, level), connected, an on_change callback, set_volume(), set_muted(), run(), and what it can do (Capabilities: volume, mute, levels). The strips show only what the provider can do.
  • BridgeProvider (implemented): the daemon serves a Unix socket; a small plugin inside the VoIP client connects and sends the participants as JSON lines, and gets the commands back. The protocol is the same for every client, so a Mumble plugin and a TeamSpeak plugin both work, and the daemon needs no client libraries. A plugin is a few hundred lines of C (Mumble's API is C) and its own build; it is not part of this phase. To try the protocol by hand, socat - UNIX-CONNECT:$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/xtouch-daemon-voip.sock and a pasted JSON line will do.
  • DemoProvider (implemented): participants from the configuration, with volume and mute kept in memory and a talking pattern, to try layouts and the strips without a VoIP client.
  • Later: TeamSpeakQueryProvider (participants and talking from ClientQuery, no volume), a Mumble plugin speaking the bridge protocol, DiscordRpcProvider only if the scope situation changes.

Bridge protocol (one JSON object per line, UTF-8):

client -> daemon  {"client": "mumble", "participants": [{"id": "12", "name": "Alice", "talking": true,
                   "muted": false, "volume": 100, "level": 0.42}], "capabilities": ["volume", "mute", "levels"]}
daemon -> client  {"set_volume": {"id": "12", "volume": 80}}
daemon -> client  {"set_muted": {"id": "12", "muted": true}}

Every client message is the whole state (like the live view): a client that sends 20 times a second while someone talks needs nothing else. volume is percent (0..200), level the peak since the last message (0..1). One client at a time; a new connection replaces the old one. The socket is mode 0600.

items.title: The Mumble plugin: mute and threads
items.text:
Mute on a voip strip is Mumble's own local mute (requestLocalMute, isUserLocallyMuted of plugin API 1.0), so Mumble shows it and a mute set in Mumble lights the button. The first version had its own mute (gain 0 in mumble_onAudioSourceFetched), because the local mute needs API calls the plugin had no safe place for:

  • Mumble calls the event callbacks in its main thread, and runs every API function there: called from another thread, it is queued to the main thread and the caller waits (Mumble's docs/dev/plugins/MumbleAPI.md, "Multithreading"). A callback that waits for a thread that waits for an API call would wait for itself, and the plugin's mumble_shutdown has to wait for its threads before Mumble unloads the library.
  • No callback comes regularly in the main thread. The talking states come only while someone talks, the users' callbacks only when someone comes or goes; a request of the daemon can wait for neither. The only timers that call plugins are those of positional audio (mumble_initPositionalData every second while no positional plugin is linked), which would make the plugin a positional one in Mumble's settings: rejected.
  • Mumble bounds the wait: a call that doesn't get to run within 800 ms is cancelled and fails with MUMBLE_EC_API_REQUEST_TIMEOUT (C_WRAPPER in src/mumble/API_v_1_x_x.cpp, the same in every release with plugin API 1.0: 1.4.230 to 1.6.870).

So the plugin has two threads: the socket thread never calls the API and only queues the mute requests (a counter per participant); the "Mumble thread" makes the requests and reads the local mute of the participants every 500 ms while the daemon is connected (Mumble has no event for it; the callbacks read it too when they refresh the users). No thread holds the plugin's lock during an API call, so a callback never waits for one. Only mumble_shutdown does: it drops the requests that have not started and waits for a call under way, which can't run then and fails after the 800 ms; the thread makes no call after that. Shutting down takes those 800 ms only if a call was under way at that moment.

While a request is under way the plugin reports the requested mute; when Mumble refuses one, it logs why (api.log) and reports Mumble's mute again, so the button goes back. A locally muted participant who talks has the talking state MUMBLE_TS_TALKING_MUTED, which counts as talking: the backlight shows it, as with the first version's mute. Their level is 0: Mumble does not mix them and fetches none of their audio.

Others' self-mute and deafen are not in the API. Plugin API 1.0 has no function for them (isLocalUserMuted and isLocalUserDeafened are the user's own), getUserComment is the free text of the user, and the talking state MUMBLE_TS_TALKING_MUTED of another user means the local mute: AudioOutputSpeech.cpp sets MutedTalking only for bLocalMute (since 1.6 also for a local volume of 0), while ClientUser::setSelfMute/setSelfDeaf emit muteDeafStateChanged, which the plugin manager doesn't forward (it connects talkingStateChanged only). Someone who muted themselves sends no audio, so they are just passive.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
Backward compatible: today's top-level [[strip]] list is the default layout, named default. A file without [[layout]] behaves exactly as before.

[[strip]]                 # the default layout, as before
type = "output"

[[strip]]
type = "apps"
label = "Browser"
match = ["firefox"]

[switching]               # optional, the defaults shown
hold = 10.0               # seconds a rule must stop matching before its layout goes
chord = [1, 8]            # Solo of strips 1 and 8 together: the next layout ([] for none)
banner = 1.5              # seconds the LCDs show the name of a new layout (0 for none)

[[layout]]
name = "gaming"           # for Home Assistant and the command line: a-z, 0-9, _
label = "Gaming"          # on the banner; by default the name
apps = ["steam_app_", ".exe"]   # rule: one of these applications has a stream (plays or paused)
processes = ["mumble"]          # rule: a process with one of these names runs
priority = 0              # of several matching layouts the highest wins, then the first in the file

[[layout.strip]]
type = "inherit"          # the strip of the default layout at this place

[[layout.strip]]
type = "apps"
label = "Game"
match = ["steam_app_", ".exe"]

[[layout.strip]]
type = "apps"
label = "VoIP"
match = ["mumble"]

[[layout.strip]]
type = "input"

[[layout.strip]]
type = "voip"             # always this person
person = ["Alice", "alice-phone"]

[[layout.strip]]
type = "voip"             # the group: the voip strips without person show the others,
[[layout.strip]]          # Select pages through more
type = "voip"

[voip]
provider = "bridge"       # or "demo"
  • Layouts are a list ([[layout]]), their order is the order of next and of the Home Assistant select.
  • Strips per layout like the top-level ones: up to 8 places, missing ones are auto. type = "inherit" takes the strip of the default layout at its place, so a shared output strip is written once. Inheriting from any layout (inherit = "music") is possible later; one level keeps it obvious.
  • Rules are part of the layout (apps, processes) rather than a separate rule list: a layout says when it applies. priority resolves overlaps.
  • Dynamic strips: every voip strip is one strip. With person it always shows that person; the others form the group of the layout, see VoIP strips: the group and fixed people. Fader: the local volume of the participant, Mute: local mute, meter: the level, the backlight turns talking_color while the participant talks.
  • Validation: names unique and not default; homeassistant ids unique per layout (a strip id used in several layouts is the same entities: one desk lamp, two layouts); voip strips need [voip].

items.title: VoIP strips: the group and fixed people
items.text:
The first version had count = N on a voip strip, which took N places. That made a strip of the file several strips of the device, which inherit, the placement of collapsing strips and the GUI all had to know about, and it gave no way to keep a person on a fader. Layouts were not released yet, so count went without a compatibility path.

[[layout.strip]]
type = "voip"
person = ["Alice", "alice-phone"]   # a fixed strip
label = "Mum"                        # by default the first name

[[layout.strip]]
type = "voip"                        # the group: all voip strips of the layout without person
  • One strip, one place. A voip strip is one strip of the layout like any other. A file with count gets the error "count is gone: write N voip strips; voip strips without person form a group".
  • Fixed strips. person is a name or a list of names of the same person, matched against the participant's name ignoring case and otherwise exactly. Wildcards were left out: names in a voice chat are chosen by people, and a pattern would sooner or later catch somebody else; aliases cover a second device. Of several participants with one of the names, the first in the provider's order is on the strip; the others go to the group, so nobody is hidden. While the person is away the strip shows its label dark with away and its fader parked, like a device that is not there; Select and Mute do nothing then. Select on a fixed strip does not page.
  • The group is every voip strip of the layout without person, in the order of the file, not necessarily next to each other. It shows the participants without a fixed strip, in the provider's order, a page at a time; Select on any of its strips shows the next page (wrapping), the LCD tells the page for 2 s (pg 2/3), and their Select LED is on while there is more than one page, as the Mackie banks do. Strips left over are dark.
  • Collapse: a strip of the group is absent while it has no participant, a fixed strip while its person is away.
  • Validation: a name on two fixed strips of one layout (after inherit) is an error; label is only for fixed strips, since a strip of the group shows the participant's name.
  • launch starts the command once per layout: the voip strips with the same command share one button (LaunchButton), so its debounce and its flashing LED are shared. launch_when_running stays off for voip strips: while the voice chat is there, Select pages.
  • Volume and mute while away. The Mumble plugin keeps them per session (a user who leaves is forgotten; one who comes back gets a new session at 100 %), and the bridge protocol has no notion of names. So the daemon keeps them: VoipProvider remembers the volume and mute the strips set by the participant's name (ignoring case) and sends them again when a participant of that name appears. A mute that changes in the client (Mumble's local mute, set in its window) replaces the kept one, so coming back does not undo it. This is for every participant, not only those of fixed strips: it costs nothing, and someone of the group who reconnects keeps their volume too. It lasts while the daemon runs; the provider survives layout switches and reloads (not a changed [voip]).
  • The live view tells the names of the participants (VoipState.names) and who each strip of the layout shown shows (VoipState.strips). The GUI suggests the names for person, its strip list says who is on which strip, and the preview prints "VOIP GROUP" or the person's name under a voip strip.

items.title: Switching
items.text:
LayoutSwitcher (src/xtouch_daemon/layouts.py) decides; the daemon carries it out.

  • Rules, edge-triggered. Every sound server snapshot and every 2 s (processes) the rules give a wanted layout: the matching layout with the highest priority, else default. When the wanted layout changes, the switcher switches to it. A layout whose rule stops matching stays for hold seconds (a game between two levels, a voice client that restarts). So the automatic switching wins when something happens, and a manual choice stays until then, like Stream Deck and Loupedeck. There is no "lock" mode yet (decided: later, see Phasing).
  • Manual: xtouch-daemon layout gaming (or --next, or without argument: list them), the GUI, the chord on the device, and Home Assistant (select.<ns>_layout). All are the same switch(name, reason).
  • Home Assistant: a select entity with the names of the layouts. The daemon publishes the active layout; a command from Home Assistant switches. Its retained state does not switch (it may be the layout of a rule of the last run): the daemon puts it right once the retained states are in.
  • Remembered across restarts (decided): the daemon keeps the layout it shows in $XDG_STATE_HOME/xtouch-daemon/layout (~/.local/state/xtouch-daemon/layout), unless a rule put it there. A switch by hand and the return of the rules to default write it, a switch by a rule does not. At the start the daemon shows it (if the configuration still has it), and the rules still win: one that matches once the sound server and the processes are known switches to its layout as usual.
  • The device: holding Solo of the chord strips together switches to the next layout. Solo does nothing on audio strips by default; on homeassistant strips the presses are still sent as events.
  • The command channel: the requests of the live view socket (those of the live preview) get one more, {"request": "layout", "layout": "gaming"} (or "+1", "-1"), answered with a reply of kind layout. The snapshot tells layout and layouts, so the GUI and the CLI see the result, and features has layout. Like the preview, the daemon takes it only from its own user (SO_PEERCRED).

items.title: On the device
items.text:
A switch is a reload with another set of strips on the same surface: the old mixer closes, a new one takes the same surface, the sound server state and the MQTT bridge. That gives the transitions for free: the faders glide to their new places, dark strips park their faders. For banner seconds the LCDs show the label of the new layout across the top lines of all 8 strips and the reason (manual, Home Assistant, an application) across the bottom lines; the strips draw underneath and appear when the banner ends. The live view shows the banner as well.

Entities in Home Assistant: the entities of the active layout are announced; those of the other layouts are kept (not removed), so automations and the entity registry don't churn on every switch. Only a reload removes entities no layout has anymore.

items.title: GUI
items.text:
• A layout bar above the strips: one tab per layout (default first), + adds one (a copy of the shown one, or empty). The preview and the strip editor show the layout of the selected tab; everything else (paths strip[3], problems, undo) works as before, for that layout. Problems of other layouts lead to them.
  • A Layout tab next to "Global settings" for the selected layout's own options (name, label, rules, priority), from the pydantic model like every other form, with buttons to move it in the order and to remove it. [switching] and [voip] are sections and get forms for free.
  • The preview is live only for the layout the device shows; another layout is shown from the file, and the bar marks the active one. A button "Show on the device" switches the daemon to the shown layout (the command channel).
  • Phase 2 for the GUI: preview of voip strips with demo participants.

items.title: Phasing
items.text:
Implemented now:

  1. Config: [[layout]], [switching], [voip], strip types inherit and voip, the default layout from [[strip]], validation; check-config shows every layout.
  2. LayoutSwitcher: rules (apps, processes) with priority and hold, manual switching, next.
  3. The daemon: switching, the banner, the chord, the command channel, xtouch-daemon layout, the select entity.
  4. VoipProvider, DemoProvider, BridgeProvider, the voip strip with paging.
  5. GUI: layout bar, layout page, live preview only for the active layout, "Show on the device".

Decided after phase 1: the Solo chord (strips 1 and 8) stays on by default, the daemon remembers the layout itself (see Switching), and Mumble is the first voice chat client with a plugin.

Later:

  • A lock mode: a manual choice that stops the rules until it is unlocked (xtouch-daemon layout --lock, a second option of the Home Assistant select or a switch next to it, a mark in the GUI's layout tabs). Deferred: the edge-triggered rules already leave a manual choice alone until something happens.
  • TeamSpeak (plugin SDK, or ClientQuery without volume). The Mumble plugin is done: integrations/mumble, see Mumble.
  • Window focus as a rule (focused = [...]) through compositor-specific providers (KWin script, Sway/Hyprland IPC).
  • Rules on time of day or on Home Assistant states (an automation can already set the select).
  • Inheriting from other layouts than the default; per-layout [behavior].
  • A GUI preview of voip strips with participants.
  • Remembering the volumes of the voice chat across restarts of the daemon.

items.title: Open questions
items.text: • Answered: a lock mode comes later; the chord is on by default; the daemon remembers the layout; Mumble first.

items.title: Design: where the people of the voice chat sit
items.text: Status: decided (2026-11-17), being built. Round 3: option D of round 2 with three built-in pools. It replaces decisions 1 and 7 of Decisions after the live test and the parts of People that place people.

items.title: Why
items.text: Until now the people of the voice chat had no candidate of their own: the resolver put them on the slots of auto, from the right, while applications filled them from the left. That fits one layout (the voice chat's strips on the right) and the file could not say anything else: not the voice chat on the left, not people in the middle, not people only in a call, not "a call replaces the applications". The GUI didn't show that auto takes people at all.

items.title: The format
items.text:
Three built-in pools. Each is a candidate like any channel or pool:

Pool Members Section and options apps The applications that play and have no channel, and the apps channels with in_pool that play and have no slot (as a whole). [pool.apps]: from (default "left"), exclude (default ["speech-dispatcher"]), hold (default 5), the look of the strips of applications on its slots. people The people in the voice chat without a person channel, and the person channels with in_pool that are present and have no slot (as themselves). In order, then as first seen (learned, kept 30 days). [pool.people]: from (default "right"), order, the look of the strips of people (color, talking_color, meter, meter_point, max_volume). auto Both: people and applications share its slots, the people first. [pool.auto]: the look of the strips of applications on its slots. People look as [pool.people] says. 
[pool.people]
from = "right"              # the side the people fill their slots from (the default)
order = ["Alice", "mum"]
color = "yellow"

[pool.apps]
from = "left"               # the default
hold = 5
exclude = ["speech-dispatcher", "notification"]

[channel.mum]
type = "person"
person = ["Alice", "alice-phone"]
in_pool = true              # while no slot shows mum, she is one of the people (default)

[slots]
4 = ["people", "apps"]      # a person, else an application
5 = ["people", { show = "apps", encoder = "pick" }]
6 = [{ show = "people", color = "orange" }, "apps"]
  • A slot without an entry is auto, and a stack that can run out ends in auto, as before. The simple case needs no words: people from the right, applications from the left, on every slot.
  • from is "left" (slot 1 first) or "right" (slot 8 first). It is an option of apps, people and the pools of channels; inside auto the people fill from [pool.people] from, the applications from [pool.apps] from. The defaults are opposite sides, so people and applications meet only when the slots run out. (Round 2 proposed "left" for every pool; with people inside auto that would make every person push the applications along.)
  • in_pool (default true) replaces in_auto: an apps channel without a slot goes into apps and auto, a person channel without a slot into people and auto.
  • Places: a place of apps takes the options of an auto place (the look, encoder, min_volume, max_volume); a place of people takes color, meter and meter_point (people show their names and have no Rec or Solo of a place).
  • Presence: present(apps) while an application apps may take plays; present(people) while someone who would be one of the people is in the voice chat (counted before slots, so also a person channel with a slot of its own); present(auto) while either is.

items.title: The rules
items.text:
Step 1 (fixed slots) and step 2 (channels by rank) stay as they are. Step 3 hands out the members of the pools.

  1. Chain. The pool a slot shows after step 2 and the candidates below it that hold while they are pools, up to and with a -, form the slot's chain. A channel ends it. ["people if call", "- if call", "auto"] while call is on: people, -.
  2. Hand-down. A pool with no member for a slot leaves it to the next pool of the chain. A slot that no pool fills shows the last pool of its chain, dark, or -. (Before: a pool slot without a member was dark.)
  3. Pools of channels first, in the order of the file, each from its side. A pool of channels below apps, people or auto in a chain is an error: those take the channels that no pool of channels gives a slot.
  4. Contest. Then the people and the applications are handed out: the people over the slots whose chain has people or auto, in their order; the applications over those with apps or auto, pins first, then each on the slot it had, then in their order. A slot both fill goes to the one higher in its stack (inside auto, the people). The other gives that slot up and is handed out again, until nothing changes. It ends: each only loses slots. Members left over wait (waiting["people"], waiting["apps"]).
  5. Fill order. Each from its side. The people first take the slots where they are the first candidate, then the others.

items.title: Not a block
items.text: People inside auto (and in people) are no block: they take the slots where nothing is above them first, then the others, each group from their side. In the live test's file with call overridden off the order was 6, 5, 4, then 8, 7, 3, 2. This stays, for a reason: people keep no slot (they sit in their order, recomputed every step), so a slot that a candidate above can take back (voip if call) would move every one of them when it does. Applications keep the slot they had, so for them the side alone decides (as before: slot 2 before slot 3, whatever is above them).

items.title: Pins, held slots, hold
items.text:
• A pin (the pick encoder) is an application's; it reserves its slot if the chain there has apps or auto. People don't take a pinned slot. People are never picked or pinned.
  • What a held or dwelling slot shows, of any pool, is not handed out again.
  • hold keeps an application a member after it stopped; absent_after keeps a person one after they left.

items.title: Use cases
items.text: A, B, ... are people in their order; "call" is the state call (Mumble: voice_chat = true). The tables come from the resolver (without a previous result).
